sections.Description:
The Stone Wall is a nice place to get away from the crowds at the Black Corridor and the Gallery.  There are many stellar climbs in the 10 range, with a few 11's. 

 The wall is east-facing, and receives some morning sun, and it often balances being just warm enough in the winter with just cool enough in the spring and fall.
sections.Getting There:
The approach is the same as for Sweet Pain Wall, but before arriving at Sweet Pain, duck left into a narrow drainage leading west. This corridor will make a 90 degree turn to the right and into the Stone Wall area. Climbs are on the left.

Alternate route description: From 2nd pull out take the main hiking trail down, at first signed intersection head uphill towards Sandstone Quarry, you'll gradually climb until a wide, flat area is reached.  Continue a short distance down (75-100 ft) on the main trail and then take a steep climber's path on the right 50-60 ft into the main wash. [This is the wash mentioned in the approach above.] Cross the main wash, looking for a path directly in front of you that enters a wash headed for the peaks. Follow this wash up. Keeping a bit to the left is easiest. The wash gradually curves back around to the right.  After 5-10 min the area flattens out into a sandy, open area. Turn left* (towards the gully that leads to Sweet Pain) and in 50-100 ft, while still in the flat, sandy area look for a 2nd branch left. Taking this will look like you're going to be "bushed out" in about 100 ft,  but the path soon reaches rock and a narrow gully-wash.  Up this to the left end of Stone Wall. 15-20 min from car.*continuing straight here, "on the flats", leads to the Black Corridor.

sections.Description: 1st route on left hand side of wall and 50 right of left facing corner.  Climb thin face past large hueco below bolted anchors.
sections.Location: 1st route on left side of cliff as you walk up from the trail.

sections.Description: Start at a left-facing flake underneath huecos.  The beginning is somewhat reachy for the vertically challanged and requires a little ingenuity.  Then things thin out and get a little cruxy before reaching the anchors.
sections.Location: This is the second route from the entrance on the wall.

sections.Description: Begins at the second left-facing flake, 5 feet right of Haunted Hooks.  Stick clipping the first bolt is recommended, as the spot from which you clip it has a slopey and somewhat sandy foot position, and I've seen someone unexpectedly come off there.  Great Red Rocks face climbing up 7 bolts through 2 cruxes.  One of the best routes on the wall!
sections.Location: The third route on the wall from the entrance, 5 feet past Haunted Hooks.

sections.Description: The start of this route is technical and uses a left facing flake which soon brings you to a right facing flake.  Many edges and seems with positive yet steep holds will bring you to the bolted summit.
sections.Location: Middle of the wall - 4th route from the left.

routes.name: Stonehenge

sections.Description: Take the lower deck and wander behind a scrub oak bush.  The start is at a deep hueco.  The route climbs steep varnished rock using scoops & thin edges.
sections.Location: 4th route from the right side of the wall.  Behind a scrub oak

routes.fa: Don Burroughs, Mike Ward & Alan Busby - '93

sections.Description: Behind a scrub oak bush and slightly right climb a thin crack system to face and anchors.
sections.Location: 3rd route from the far right and just right/behind a scrub oak bush.

sections.Description: Start route off boulder and right facing flake. Climb the thin varnished wall to shared anchor.
sections.Location: Second route from right
sections.Protection: 6 bolts to shared anchors (shares with Stone Hammer II)

sections.Description: The furthest right climb on the wall.  The start involves a little weirdness, and it just continues, all the way up.  Climb up lower angle rock to a large dish.  Pull the dish on the left (awkward!) and continue up to anchors.
sections.Location: last route on the Stone Wall.
sections.Protection: 6 bolts plus whatever you like to put on bolted anchors

sections.Description: The Great Red Book Rock is most well known for the Great Red Book route that follows up a glorious dihedral on the left side of the crag. The rock, a giant slab, is visible from the parking lot, above and to the right of the Hunter S. Thompson Dome. Facing west, it gets a lot of sun after noon. In addition to the dihedral route which is a 5.8 trad route, there are several mixed and sport routes on the vast face 5.8 - 5.11. The routes end up almost at the top of the Calico formations, where you can get a killer view of the canyons to the west.
sections.Getting There: To get to the Great Red Book Rock, first head to the Black Corridor area from the Second Pullout parking lot. Go through the corridor and hang a hard right up the ramp that skirts below the Hunter S. Thompson Dome. Pass the Dome and Poser Crag and head left up the talus slope to the base of crag.

sections.Description: Start up the neat column of rock with the porthole behind it. Fight through some steep crimps for a few more moves, then onto slab and a steep wall above with the anchors. Note: there is some soft rock on this route that will continue to clean up with ascents, use helmets.
sections.Location: Far left end of GRB area, 20' from where the walk-off emerges back to the font of the cliff. Look for a column of rock with a 2-foot hole behind it.

sections.Description: Climbs up a slightly overhanging corner and bulge on good holds. Above the bulge is some low-angle slab to a couple vertical headwalls with big holds.
sections.Location: Located about 25' left of the Liner at a slightly overhung crack/seam with a 2-foot roof on the right.

sections.Description:
Located high up on the left, north-facing side of GRB area. Best accessed after climbing to the big ledge of the route Collaborative Overlap, or after topping out the GRB formation and walking off. Look to the skier's left as you scramble down the walk-off.
Climb up a blocky inside-corner to gain a slightly left-angling crack in a shallow open-book. Getting established in the crack is the crux and has a bolt to prevent decking. As the crack runs out, climb up the low-angle corner to bolted ring anchors. Too bad the crack proper isn't longer as it dies just as it really gets going. Three bolts and a few finger-sized cams to 1". Good beginner trad climb akin to pitches encountered in the canyons that won't have bolts.Rappel or... From here a couple fifth class moves will get you to a huge ledge with large boulders. Walk off of this ledge to the left and join the GRB walkoff, or top out the formation with an easy scramble up the corner behind the boulders.
sections.Protection: Gear to 1" and some bolts. Bolted rap anchors.

sections.Description: Located up high on the far left, north-facing side of the GRB formation. Best reached by climbing the first two pitches of Collaborative Overlap to the big ledge with anchors. From here move 50' around the corner to the left and look for the bolt line of the first pitch.P1: 5.8, 60', 8 b. Climb up the face to a ledge on the right, then up the right-side of the blunt arete (crux) to quick-clip anchors. Another pitch to add before you finish climbing Collaborative Overlap.P2: 5.5, 90’, Single rack to 2". Kinda crappy, but easy and it'll go to the top. Above the anchors is a small ledge and a low-angle crack. Follow it to its end and continue up the unprotected, but easy climb-walking to the anchors of Collaborative Overlap.
sections.Protection: First pitch: fully bolted with quick-clip anchors. Second pitch: gear to 2" then runout to the top.

sections.Description: A big, right-facing corner. Climb to the top of the corner (50') then you have options: traverse up and right to the Liner and it's anchors, or continue around the top of the corner to the left and up another 50' through some ledges to a walk-off. Mind the rope drag.
sections.Location: About 200' left of the Great Red Book corner and 10' left of the Liner.
sections.Protection: Single rack with emphasis on bigger gear to 5".

sections.Description: Climbs the straight, slightly right-angling handcrack on the left side of the rock.  It's a pretty straightforward climb, with plenty of gear in the crack and featured rock on the face. This route appears in Handren's 2007 Guidebook.
sections.Location: About 150' left of The Great Red Book proper.
sections.Protection: Singles to 3" should do it. The anchors are off to the right on a ramp, so make sure to extend your last piece. There are quicklinks, not rap rings, so make sure to rappel instead of lowering if you don't want to pig-tail your rope.

sections.Description: Another beginner lead route with mostly 5.easy climbing and one 5.7 crux move. Start at a chocolate varnish patch about 10’ right of the right-angling crack of the Liner. Climb up the varnish patch and onto the steeper wall above. Continue straight up to an anchor at a bulge. Note: there is some delicate rock off the bolt line so be careful while lowering
sections.Location: Located about 10' right of the Liner at a low-angle, chocolate varnish patch.

sections.Description: A nice beginner lead. Mostly 5.5 climbing with a single 5.7 crux move. Start at a right-angling seam/ramp about 20’ right of the right-angling crack of the Liner. Climb up the face to where it meets a ramp from the left. Step onto the ramp and continue up the face through lots of varnish holds. End at anchors atop a large black varnish patch.
sections.Location: Start at a right-angling seam/ramp between The Liner and Collaborative Overlap on the left side of GRB.

sections.Description: This route is just to the right of Liner. You might not have noticed it because the first bolt is way up there. Not like the normal clip-up RR sport routes. Just 3 bolts. Goes through fun plate pulling on mostly good rock, but still a little crumbly. You might be able to get a nut or chicken head for pro, but the patina was a little brittle, so it probably wouldn’t hold a whip. Anyone know FA info?
sections.Location: Left side of Great Red Book area between Liner and Reservations Required.
sections.Protection: 3 bolts to chain anchor. Bolts and anchor look good.

sections.Description:
Start about 30' right of The Liner, climb up and right to an optional anchor then up the low-angle rock to a big ledge below a headwall. There's a couple lines up the headwall to the top or you can walk off from the big ledge. Depending on the route taken on the headwall, and linked pitches or not, this climb can be 2-4 pitches. Fully bolted. Use the GRB walkoff from the top.P1: 5.7, 45', 5 b. Climb up 15' and trend right following bolts to a longboard-sized ledge with optional belay at the 6th bolt.P2: 5.7+, 90', 8 b. Head up the short, shallow crack, then up the slab to anchors on a big ledge below the vertical headwall. There is some soft rock around bolt 7 so climb with care as this cleans up.Pitches 3/4 go up the headwall, above the big ledge, to the top. Described here is the original line of this route which is left of the anchor. Right of the anchor is the route Cognitive Overload (10b).P3: 5.10a/b, 65', 9 b. From the anchor on the big ledge, move left and climb up the shallow open-book/corner. At its end, traverse left a few feet and climb through a bulge to better holds above. A tricky/reachy move (crux) gains a skateboard-sized ledge and optional belay at the 10th bolt. Note: Above this point, the large ledge and belayer below are out of sight as the steepness tapers off and rope drag may be an issue.P4: 5.6, 60', 3b. A few easy moves lead to low-angle, climb-walking to the top where anchors anxiously await your arrival.
Descent: Use the GRB walkoff from the top.
sections.Location: Located on the far left side of the Great Red Book area, between Reservations Required and The Liner.

sections.Description:
Starts immediately right of the anchors on the big ledge reached by climbing the first two pitches of Collaborative Overlap. Get established on the wall with the dark-varnish hold and dyno (or don't) to the jug rail. Crimp, side-pull, and pinch your way up the wall to bolt 11 (~70') where there is a quick-clip anchor. Above this point the steepness tapers off to shared anchors with Collaborative Overlap at the top. 120', 13b.
I suggest adding this climb as an extra pitch while doing Collaborative Overlap. Use the anchors at ~70' to avoid the rope drag of going to the top.
sections.Location: Climb Collaborative Overlap to the big ledge halfway up the wall. That route continues up to the left of the anchor. Cognitive Overload goes up just right of the anchor.
sections.Protection: 10 bolts to a quick-clip anchor. 13 bolts total if you go to the top.

sections.Description: Climb up the smooth, beautiful black varnish face to the left of RR. There are perfect varnish crimps to the left of the bolt line, and the smooth frictionless slab on the right is a fun TR challenge (albeit harder than 5.9).
sections.Location: Located just left of the left-angling corner first pitch of Reservations Required.

sections.Description:
Waiting in line for GRB? You brought all your quickdraws/alpine-draws right? This climb will warm ya up. First pitch is sport-bolted with quick-clip anchors. Pitches 2 and 3 feature larger spacing on the easier terrain. Linking pitches, if you must, will incur rope drag for days.
P1: 5.10a. Follow the bolts up the beautiful chocolatey corner to an anchor on a nice ledge. 40', 5 bolts with quick-clips. Crux move around bolt 4.

P2: 5.9. Follow bolts mostly straight up the low-angle wall through two steep sections: A slight overhang, and a vertical headwall just below the anchors on another nice ledge. (The rock right below the mantle to the anchor ledge is soft, climb carefully.) 130', 13 bolts.

P3: 5.8. Follow the bolts climbing the nose-bridge right between the huge, hueco-eyesockets. Anchors are at the top of the formation. 80', 6 bolts.
Descent: Use the walkoff for GRB. You can rappel the route with a 70m rope (70m is mandatory) if you have to, but just walk off.
sections.Location: Located 100' left of GRB. Find the obvious smooth, darkly-varnished, slab/scoop with a left-angling diagonal corner. The route starts on the right end of this corner. Scramble up easy 4th class to a nice ledge to begin.
sections.Protection: Fully bolted. Quick-clips on the first pitch anchors.

sections.Description:
Fun slab with an exciting roof pull located between GRB and RR. Starts on a nice ledge that is about 15' up so be careful getting set up. Mostly bolted with a run out or optional gear on last 50' of easy, climb-walking on second pitch.
Pitch 1: 5.8+, 105', 10 bolts (+1 belayer bolt). After the first lead-bolt, mantle to a sloping-ledge and move left to the next bolt. Continue up through mostly low-angle rock with good holds which gets steeper and better the higher you go. End at a small but decent ledge with anchor bolts.Pitch 2: 5.9, 125', 9 bolts, optional gear. Climb up the short, shallow right-facing corner and onto the slab above. Continue up the slab aiming for the 3-foot, right-facing arete/corner/roof above. Pull through this feature, trending left above, to a small ledge with a left-facing corner (you can't see this corner from the belay). The rock between the last bolt and the small ledge is a little crispy still, climb carefully as this section cleans up. All bolt protected to this point and business has largely concluded. 80' to this small ledge.
Once on the ledge, you won't be able to see your follower and you can do an optional gear anchor if desired. That said, I suggest avoiding this belay, extend any pro placed above, and just climb-walk up the easy corner (5.2) to the top. The anchor is in a microwave-sized hueco to the right of the crack just before the summit's flat top. 50'. Finger/hand-size gear for the optional belay/pro (long runners/slings helpful).Note: I found the existing top anchors midway through developing the route. If anyone has any knowledge of this and wants credit given, please let me know.
sections.Location: Located about 40' left of GRB. Scramble up a left-facing corner to the right end of a ledge with a scraggly Cat's Claw bush on the left end. Centered on the ledge is a belayer-bolt which marks the start of the route.
sections.Protection: Bolts and optional gear on the 50' of easy climbing to the top. Bolted anchors.

routes.name: Great Red Book

sections.Description:
This is a great route and the site of the rappelling error that led to the fate of renowned Red Rock climber and guide Randal Grandstaff.
The location of this climb is obvious. It more or less climbs the giant left facing dihedral, aka The Great Red Book...
P1 (5.8): Climb up past a few vegetated ledges and work over into the corner proper for about 10-15 ft. When the crack becomes too thin, head back out onto the face and up to the bolted anchor where a memorial for Randall has been scratched into the rock (technically this is a chipped route :)
P2 (5.8 PG): Climb up the face on small edges past 2 bolts and lieback around the OW in the corner. Shoot for the top via the face or chimney.
Descend by heading down and right initially, then back left through a notch, following frequent cairns to a gully. Easy scrambling returns you to the base of the wall.

routes.fa: Bob Logerquist and John Williamson, Oct 1971

routes.name: Bury the Hatchet

sections.Description:
Although only 50' long, Bury the Hatchet has great moves and achieves a rather spectacular position.  Well worth climbing if you're  up at the Great Red Book. 

 Climb the first pitch of that route (5.7), and belay.  From the anchor, continue up 20' to the weakness in the steep right wall of the Book.  After making a reachy clip, unleash the fury and perform a burly hand traverse on decent holds past two more bolts before rocking up onto an exposed perch on the arete. 

 Belay here off bolts and either continue with the final 5.10a pitch of Animal Boy or lower/rap back to the first anchor of the Great Red Book.  One more 100' rap takes you to the ground. 

 This project was envisioned, equipped, and graciously opened by Josh Thompson.
sections.Protection: A light rack for the Great Red Book and three draws (optional 0.5 Camalot with a long sling protects making the first clip).

routes.fa: FFA: Joshua Janes & Andy Hansen - November 2011FA: Josh Thompson, Joanne & Danny Urioste - September 2011

sections.Description:
Climbs 3 pitches up the left-end of the right-side of the GRB area. Start at a left-facing corner about 20’ right of the arete route, Animal Boy. The first pitch is a great single pitch on its own. 
All anchors are fitted with pigtail lower-offs if needed, but if you go to the top please walk off. This is not a good climb to rappel as the varnish jugginess will snag your rope!  It’s quick and easy as it follows the GRB walk-off. It's 10 min back to the base of the wall.
Bring 11 quickdraws plus your anchor. A 60m rope will suffice.
P1: 5.10d, 8b, 70': Scramble up into the left-facing corner and climb it’s right-side trending up and right. As the corner closes out and the wall steepens, continue straight up for a couple bolts. Continue following bolts back left (crux) through the blank, improbable-looking wall to anchors at a semi-hanging belay. A great pitch! Note: About halfway up, the route converges a bit with the route to the right, use caution if other climbers are present.
P2: 5.8, 9b, 70': Climb straight up from the anchors past a horizontal band of black varnish and a slight bulge. Above the bulge trend leftward and up the slab to anchors at a small ledge.
P3: 5.10a, 11b, 110': Climb up the slab to the steep headwall forming the upper cap of rock to the wall. Follow bolts up the steepness for 20’ (crux) and continue up the easy slab above as the angle eases to a great ledge at the top. Use the left anchors.
sections.Location: About 40' right of the book itself. Look for a left-facing corner with a smooth, blank varnished wall on the left and some boulders at the base.

sections.Description:
Climbs 3 pitches to the top of the formation that makes the right-side of GRB. Start about 50' right and below the book. Bring 13 quickdraws. A 60m rope will work to lower/rappel the first pitch if you move left as you lower. Be mindful of climbers on Zero Shot as the plumb line of the first pitch anchors overlaps at the crux of that route! 
Anchors are fitted with pigtail lower-offs, but if you go to the top please walk off. It’s quick and easy as it follows the GRB walk-off. This is not a good climb to rappel. The traversing nature means you’re likely to rap onto other climbs and the varnish jugginess will snag your rope!
P1: 5.9, 13b, 110': Climb up the blank slab, past an overlap, and onto low-angle slab above. Continue up through some beautiful, black varnish to a bulge and shallow left-facing roof/flake above. Climb past the roof/flake and angle up and left to the anchors at a small ledge. Follow the silver bolts. Note: About halfway up, the route converges a bit with the routes on either side, use caution if other climbers are present.
P2: 5.8, 12b, 95': Climb straight up from the anchors past the right edge of a horizontal band of black varnish. Continue up past a horizontal overlap to a slab/bulge that eases into a sloping ledge below the base of the upper headwall and the anchors.
P3: 5.10b, 10b, 85': Climb up the vertical headwall (crux) onto lower-angle rock above. The upper portion of the pitch angles to the left where the anchors are on a nice ledge at the top of the formation (next to the anchors for the route to the left, Zero Shot). Use the anchors on the right.
sections.Location: Located about halfway between the mushroom boulder and the Book itself at a glue-in bolt in the middle of a low-angle, smooth slab behind a 4-5’ boulder pile. There are two bolt lines near-ish each other, Dreamstate is the line of silver glue-in bolts on the left.

sections.Description:
Climbs two pitches up to the base of the upper headwall at the top of the right/south side of the GRB formation. Start about 25’ left of the mushroom boulder at a left-facing flake behind some boulders. Anchors are fitted with pigtail lower-offs for easy rappelling down. That said, the varnish jugginess on the route will do its best to snag your rope! Bring 13 quickdraws and a 70m rope.
A nice 2-pitch route showcasing much of the typical climbing in Red Rock: varnish jugs, crimps, and a some friction slab, all with a great view!
P1: 5.8, 13b, 110': Climb the flake up to and over a slight bulge at its top. Continue up some slab passing to the right of a black varnish patch to steeper rock above. Next, climb the crux and into easier climbing along the right side of a crack/seam up to the anchors at a small ledge. Note: About halfway up, the route converges a bit with the route to the left, use caution if other climbers are present.
P2: 5.8, 11b, 90': Climb straight up off the anchor through some varnish jugginess to some easy slab climbing to the top. Anchors are at the base of a 4’ black varnish patch.
Rappel the route.
sections.Location: Located about 25' left of the mushroom boulder at a left-facing flake behind some boulders.

routes.name: Tomato Amnesia

sections.Description:
Start just left of the mushroom boulder, aiming for a bolt 20' above. Climb up and right, then left to the base of a curving crack. Follow the crack to an anchor, having clipped five bolts getting to and into the crack.  
      The second pitch follows the crack up the short steep wall, then up the slab to an anchor with chains at a horizontal seam. Another bolt above the belay invites further climbing.... new hardware to us.  
      There is a fragile flake left of the crack, between the two bolts, that will last as long as no one pulls out on it.  
       Handren's guide rates the second pitch at 5.5. We thought it significantly harder.
sections.Location: The route is on the wall right of Great Red Book. There are bolts all over the place, but you are left of the mushroom and some small scrub oaks.
sections.Protection: Stoppers, tcu's,  and small cams to #1 Cam. 5 bolts first pitch, 2 on second.

routes.fa: Don Wilson, Karen Wilson, and Jack Marshall, Mar 1988

sections.Description:
Climbs two pitches up to the base of the upper headwall at the top of the right/south-side of the GRB formation. Start directly behind the mushroom boulder at a smooth, shallow, black-varnish corner. Anchors are fitted with pigtail lower-offs for easy rappelling.
Bring 16 quickdraws and your anchor. An 80m rope is ideal for the first pitch, but a 70m will work with minimal shenanigans if you lower to the right. Watch your rope ends!
P1: 5.10a, 16b, 125': Start up the smooth, shallow corner and follow bolts climbing through jugs and delicate moves alike. Continue up through the black varnish crack/seam at the top. A long pitch that can be done with a 70m rope, but you will need to lower to the right to reach the small ledge about 10’ up on the route, See Spot Run.
P2: 5.9+, 11b, 80’: Climb straight up off the anchor through some delicate moves passing a bulge and onto the slab above. Continue up the slab to anchors at the base of the upper headwall.
Lower/rappel the route.
sections.Location: Located directly behind the mushroom boulder at a smooth, shallow, black-varnish corner.

sections.Description: See Spot run is an fun little climb originally with a 30' run-out. With Mark's blessing the route has been updated with more bolts for leaders at its grade. Climb up the slabby face behind the mushroom boulder to an anchor with a pigtail lower-off.
sections.Location: Approach as per "Great Red Book". "See Spot Run" is the second route on the huge ledge to the right of the book itself. Locate a mushroom-shaped boulder and a scrub oak bush against the wall to the right of the boulder. The route is dead center of the two features.

sections.Description: Start by the mushroom boulder just right of See Spot Run and climb to bolt 40' up, then a 30' runout to two bolts a few inches apart below a seam. Continue up the thin seam to a slung bolts anchor. 70m rope required.
sections.Location: Start behind the mushroom shaped boulder just right of See Spot Run.
sections.Protection: Small stuff- rp's, ballnutz, and slings to wrap plates.

sections.Description: Start immediately right of the scrub oak bushes to the climber’s right of the mushroom boulder. Follow the line of glue-in bolts to anchors about 10’ below the shared anchors of the routes, Chips Ahoy and the extension of Elementary Primer. If you have a 70m you can extend the climb up to the higher anchors using the last pro bolt of the Elementary Primer extension. A nice route with mostly 5.8 or easier climbing and a single, thin 5.9 crux move.
sections.Location: Located between See Spot Run and Elementary Primer (to the right of the run-out Chips Ahoy). Starts immediately right of the scrub oak bushes to the climber's right of the mushroom boulder on the right side of the GRB area.

sections.Description:
Start at a 4', left-facing flake above some scrub oak. Climb up slab to a crux bulge at about halfway, then some friction moves before gaining the varnished jugs to the anchor. With Mark's blessing this route was updated with more bolts to be more approachable to leaders at its grade (thanks Mark!). The original three Metolius bolts are still in use if you want the OG experience.
There is a 5 bolt (glue-ins) extension that goes up and left, and meets the recently replaced glue-in anchor on Chips Ahoy. This extension goes at about 10a and is 115', watch your rope ends.
sections.Location: Elementary Primer starts about 40' right of the mushroom boulder and 10' left of the start of the corridor that forms betweens the ledge and the wall, where Stone Hammer. and Seams Novel begin.

sections.Description: Start up a right-leaning seam and continue straight up (staying left of the seam) after the fourth bolt. Head straight up to another bolt 25' higher and pass the original anchors of Seams Novel on the left of the scoop. Continue up through some varnish cracks passing another bolt and finish up on a seam to the left or straight up running it out either way to the top. Belay on less than inspiring gear options or use one of the bolted anchors from another route.
sections.Location: About 50' feet right of the Great Red Book. Walk off to the west.
sections.Protection: 7 bolts total including one from the original anchor of Seams Novel. Single rack to hands, slings for chickenheads. Handren recommends RP's but I used none.

sections.Description: So this route is an extension to Seams Novel 5.8, from the anchors you want to traverse left to move into the most prominent crack inside of the varnished flaked wall. From here you can protect the climb with a .75 cam and sling a chickenhead, move on up 20 ft and sling your last chickenhead and get ready for a runout of 40 ft on 5.6 slab climbing without pro placement and very mental and airy. Keep on trudging straight up until you hit a brittle ledge with a slanting seam where you build your anchor with #3, #2, #1 or .75 cams. The descent is the as for Great Red Book.
sections.Location: About 150+/- feet right of the Great Red Book. Walk off to the west.
sections.Protection: 3 bolts and single cam rack to hands; also can sling some chickenheads.

sections.Description:
Seams Novel climbs the obvious right-angling seam to a 10' varnish filled scoop. The original single pitch anchor is on the left side of this scoop. A 30' extension continues when the seam ends to an anchor at 105'. A second pitch goes up to the top of the wall. With Mark's blessing, this route has been updated with more bolts to make it more approachable to leaders at its grade (thanks Mark!).
Pitch 1: 5.8, 9b total to OG anchor on left. 3 bolt extension to anchor at 105'.
Pitch 2: 5.8-, 90', 8b to chain anchor at the top. 
Descent: Rappel or use GRB walkoff.
sections.Location: This route climbs the right-leaning seam of Stone Hammer in its entirety. When the seam ends head left to the OG anchor or continue up to an anchor above the scoop. Another pitch goes to the top.

sections.Description: Start in the 8 foot deep crevice that forms just right of the start of Seams Novel at a right-facing flake. Follow bolts up and slightly right through varnish jugs to an anchor just below a steep, blank bulge.
sections.Location: About 50' right of the mushroom boulder and 15' right of the right-leaning seam of Seams Novel in an 8' deep crevice next to the wall.

sections.Description: Chips Away is the runout route between Seams Novel/Epilogue routes and Ground Up Vocab. Start in the corridor formed by the ledge and the wall about 10' left of the small pine tree. It climbs the steep, blank slabby wall with a bolt at 40' just below a horizontal stripe of varnish. There are 2 more bolts through the steep bulge above to a tat anchor on bolts. A second pitch continues climbing up the face past one bolt to the top. Be careful of some loose rock below the top. A decent gear belay can be found in a left facing corner, or you could use one of the bolted anchors of another route.
sections.Location: About 80' right of the mushroom boulder where a steep step-across gains the higher base-ledge, step down into the corridor formed by the ledge and the wall. Pick your favorite spot along the corridor to start and aim for the lone bolt below the varnish horizontal stripe.
sections.Protection: Bolts, small cams/nuts. Gear is minimal and lousy.

sections.Description:
Start in the corridor formed by the base-ledge separating from the wall, directly behind the small pine tree. Stem/chimney up 10' out of the corridor and get established on the face at the first glue-in bolt. Thin/delicate climbing gets you to some jugs at the first mechanical bolt. This is the original first bolt on the route. Follow the bolts trending rightward through a varnish patch and a bulge to lower angle climbing just below the anchor (shared with Dangling Participles). A second pitch climbs to an anchor on a ledge/cave just below the top.
Mark bolted this route ground-up and all original mechanical bolts were preserved if you want the OG experience. With Mark's blessing this route was updated with more bolts (glue-ins) for us mortal leaders.
Pitch 1: 5.8+, 105', 12b, chain anchor with small ledge.
Pitch 2: 5.7, 60', 7b, chain anchor at the top.
Descent: Rappel or use GRB walkoff.
sections.Location: About 100' to the right of the mushroom boulder in front of the small pine tree at the high point of the base-ledge.

sections.Description:
A great route that is very similar to subject verb agreement on this same wall. The route is actually two pitches with the second pitch shared with Ground Up Vocab route that joins the first pitch anchor from the left.
Start in the corridor at the base of the wall and follow lots of bolts up to shared anchors with GUV. Some interesting and enjoyable moves at the grade make for a really nice route.
sections.Location: This route is on the sunny Great Red Book Wall, about 100 yards right of the Great Red Book itself.  It is about 40 feet left of Subject Verb Agreement and directly above a great belay spot to hide from the sun.  You can reach it by hiking around on a ledge below the face, and into a 8' deep gully between the ledge and face. This climb is 20 feet left of a place where it is easy to step down into the gully. Follow the obvious line of bolts!
sections.Protection: First pitch is about 12-13 draws with fixed anchors. The second pitch is shared with Ground Up Vocab and has 7 bolts to chain anchors.

sections.Description:
Named for our president, who often ignores this rule of grammar: "Families is where our nation finds hope, where wings take dream." (George W. Bush, 2000) 

 This route is not the right-most on the cliff, but it is the farthest right route that contains a significant number of bolts.  This is one of the few routes on this crag that is not runout.
sections.Location: This route is about 100 yards right (south) of the Great Red Book.  Hike around on a ledge below the face, soon a gully forms between the ledge and the face.  Climb down into it, and look for the last set of bolts, the first one just above a black, varnished section.

sections.Description:
The Black Corridor is an extremely popular area for 5.9-5.11 sport climbing. Usually shady apart from midday when the sun shines directly down into the corridor, this area tends to have it's own micro climate and is sheltered from the wind and climbable year-round.
Human waste is a major problem here: You'll notice the smell of urine as you enter the corridor as well as a Wag bag dispenser. Please use the Wag bags or return to the trailhead bathroom. If you have to urinate, please walk much further than "around the corner" to do your business.
The corridor can become extremely crowded - a little courtesy (keeping your equipment organized and out of the way of traffic, using your indoor voices, and keeping your children, pets, and significant others under control are all greatly encouraged).
The area is subdivided into two main sections (the upper and lower levels) which are separated by a pile of boulders.
sections.Getting There:
Follow the trail from the parking lot until it drops down into the lower wash. Continue walking through the wash and up and over slickrock passing several pools of water to another wash. Cross this sandy wash to another rib of slickrock. Up and over this into a narrow wash which is followed to the entrance to the lower level.
0.3 mi and 50 feet of elevation gain, 5-10 minutes.

sections.Description:
This is the lower level of the Black Corridor, separated from the upper level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble. 

 The area is subdivided left and right, as viewed from the entrance to the corridor looking towards upper level.
sections.Getting There: See parent area for approach instructions. This is the first area reached from the approach.

sections.Description:
This is the lower level of the Black Corridor, separated from the upper level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble.  

 These routes are on the left side as viewed from the entrance to the corridor looking towards upper level.
sections.Getting There: The wall on the left (southwest) side of the lower level.

sections.Description: This climb is more slabby in nature than the other routes in the corridor. No one move is a crux, but several of the moves require balance.
sections.Location: This is now the first route on the left as you enter the corridor. This line was bolted after Roxanna's new guide was published, so it is not included in her topo.
sections.Protection: Several bolts to a shiny new chain anchor.

sections.Description:
AKA Left #2
Crimpy start to a series of large flakes. Steeper finish on positive holds. This one is somewhat sparsely bolted and has a few committing moves.
sections.Location: Second route on the left as you enter the corridor.

sections.Description:
This is a new route in the corridor- the third on your left as you enter the lower tier, it ascends an obvious line of features.  

Care should be taken on this route as many of the features are hollow and the route is still shedding rock. The bolts are also spaced somewhat, so be mindful.
sections.Location: Third route on left.

routes.name: Bonaire

sections.Description: Bonaire is the fourth route on the left (lower level) route encountered in the Black Corridor.  Climb through 6 or 7 bolts to a fixed anchor at the top.
sections.Protection: 7 bolts to lower-off anchors. The first bolt can be skipped as it is not in line with the climbing.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Bon Ez

sections.Description: Bon Ez is the second route on the left (lower level) encountered in the Black Corridor.  Climb through 7 or 8 bolts to a fixed anchor at the top.
sections.Protection: Quickdraws, fixed anchors at the top.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Crude Boys

sections.Description: The climb just right of Bonaire/Bon Ez.  I seem to recall it being pretty contrived, with the crux down low on steep, thin rock.
sections.Protection: A few bolts to a lower-off.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

sections.Description:
AKA "Black Corridor #4."
Distinct crux around the second bolt on quality varnish. Easier climbing above.

routes.name: Unnamed (Black Corridor #5)

sections.Description: A trad line in the Black Corridor? Yup. This route is on the left side of the lower section about 20 feet left of the boulders in the middle of the corridor. Start by clipping a bolt and head for the thin crack to the top. Build an anchor with gear and walk off right.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Vagabonds

sections.Description: Vagabonds is located on the left side of the lower section of the Black Corridor. Close to the boulders that separate the two tiers, on the left side, there is a trad route, BCR 5L. Its most prominent feature is a large crack up high. Vagabonds is the next route to the right from the crack. The 5.10a rating can be mitigated a bit by wandering a little and seeking an easier path. Lower off with one rope.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Crude Control

sections.Description: Really kind of a bomb because of its contrived nature, not because of the rock.  Beginning right of Vagabonds (but left of the boulders that separate the corridor) this route starts up a short steep section involving a move from a digit hold to a shelf above.  Can be easily cheated by just reaching right for a ramp and climbing via that.  Two bolts protect the crux, with 5 more to the anchors.

routes.fa: Steagall, Sandefur, Werner, and Sobocan, Fall 1990

sections.Description:
This is the lower level of the Black Corridor, separated from the upper level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble.  

 These routes are on the right side, as viewed from the entrance to the corridor looking towards upper level.
sections.Getting There: The wall on the right (northeast) side of the lower level.

sections.Description: This route starts out climbing a right leaning crack  (crux) and continues through some large huecos and ledges.  In the Handren guidebook, this route is referred to as "Need to Rest," but Mike's original name was Idiot Parade.
sections.Location: This is the last route on the right side of the lower corridor, if you enter from the bottom. It is located just before the dividing boulders.

routes.name: Friend

sections.Description: Lots of big holds, lots of big rests.  Climb the Hueco over a bulge.  Bring a coffee for those no hands rests--don't be afraid to get up in that hueco and shake em out.
sections.Location: Lower corridor, right side.  Directly behind that lonely shrubby tree.

routes.fa: Richard Harrison, Lisa Harrison, and Michelle Locatelli, May 2006

routes.name: Foe

sections.Description: Big holds, a good rest.  Past a big scoop over a bulge to a small mantle.
sections.Location:
Just right of Friend and just left of Nightmare on crude street in the lower corridor, right side.. 

 Find the shrubby tree in the center of the corridor.

routes.fa: Richard Harrison, Lisa Harrison, and Michelle Locatelli, May 2006

routes.name: Nightmare on Crude Street

sections.Description: One of the better climbs in the corridor - It's not loose like the guide indicates.  This climbs the huge hueco system directly across from the Bon- climbs.  Crux is a tough step right about halfway up.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

sections.Description: Climb up nice edges and sloping huecoes to a right trending seam/crack.  Pull over a small lip (crux) and climb varnish crimps to chains.
sections.Location: The route between Nightmare on Crude Street and The Heavy Hitter.

sections.Description:
I was told that the first ascensionist wanted to rate this climb 5.11a. I am not sure if a final rating has been decided, but I consider it to be a mid-range 5.10. 

 There is a tricky sequence at the bottom of this route (smearing feet), followed by easier climbing. This second "crux" involves moving through some huge huecos near the top. If you proceed left through the huecos the climbing is easier, but more reachy; proceed to the right, and you have a few harder moves but they are very straight forward.
sections.Location: This line was bolted after Roxanna's new guide was published, so it is not included in her topo. It is the fifth route on the right as you enter the corridor from the lower approach, and starts in a right-facing scooped corner.
sections.Protection: Several bolts to the shiny new chains.

routes.name: She's Deadly

sections.Description: Easier climbing leads to a good rest before a brief but intense crux.
sections.Location: 2 feet past the small tree, there is a small lip that travels up from the ground and a prominent hole 8 feet off the ground.

routes.fa: Richard Harrison, Lisa Harrison, and Michelle Locatelli, Oct 2007

routes.name: M & M

sections.Description: Just to the right of The Heavy Hitter 5.10c and between two small trees is a relatively new route called M & M that goes at about 5.11-. Cruxy from the third to the fourth bolt and a steep finish to the anchors. It's still a bit chossy from he fourth to the seventh bolt but it should clean up with traffic.
sections.Location: The sixth route on the lower right side of the corridor just past Michael Angelo 5.11a on the lower right side. It starts between two small trees just left of a right-arching flake.

routes.fa: Dan Meyers and Rob Mansfield, Feb 2007

sections.Description: Starts off fun and easy with interesting holes and huecos to use, gets more difficult midway through as the holds become smaller. The crux seems to be clipping the anchors at the little headwall at the top - started out easy,but many of the original holds I used when I did the first ascent have vanished. I named it as a memorial to my bro Mike who I lost this year, a hero to me.
sections.Location: The route is the fifth one up on the right lower side as you are coming into the corridor. It is between Psychobilly and M & M. It starts at the first small tree. Please take care not to injure tree.
sections.Protection: There are seven bolts and chain anchors.

routes.name: Psychobilly

sections.Description: This route is awesome!  Probably one of the top four routes in the corridor if you can climb at this grade. Climb the easy holds up to the third bolts and then crimp your way to a great left handed undercling. This will require smearing you feet on the way up. There is a two finger pocket for your right hand, followed by a few more crimps as you move upward. The top section to the anchors is relatively easy climbing after the crux.
sections.Location: This line was bolted after Roxanna's new guide was published, so it is not included in her topo. It is the fourth route on the right as you enter the corridor from the lower approach, and follows the obvious thin crack to a huge undercling flake.
sections.Protection: Seven bolts to the new chain anchor.

routes.fa: Richard Harrison, Lisa Harrison and Michelle Locatelli, May 2006

routes.name: Burros Might Fly

sections.Description:
Descent moves up descent rock. Climb the thin edges after the ramp, and run it out across a flake to the fourth bolt. 

 Both 'Burros' climbs receive afternoon sun so plan to climb them when you're looking for some rays!  =)
sections.Location: This route is the third in from the entrance of the corridor. Start by climbing the right leaning ramp to the first bolt, then continue straight up.
sections.Protection: Several bolts up to an anchor (This anchor used to be shared with Burros Don't Gamble, but now has its own).

routes.fa: Harrison Shull, Todd Hewitt, and Dane Cox, Dec 1994

routes.name: Burros Don't Gamble

sections.Description: Burros Don't Gamble is the second route on the right (lower level) of the Black Corridor.  It has a tree just to the right of the route if I remember correctly.  Climb through cool huecos clipping 7 or 8 bolts, passing the crux down low.  Rap from a fixed anchor.

routes.fa: Harrison Shull and Todd Hewitt, Dec 1994

sections.Description: Climb starts next to a tree and the new wag bag dispenser. The route everyone misses and confuses with burros don't gamble. Approx 80 feet long. This climb is better than it appears lots of fun sequences and interesting holds. Some decent rests between thin technical climbing.
sections.Location: First route on right when you enter canyon

sections.Description:
This is the upper level of the Black Corridor, separated from the lower level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble.  

 The area is subdivided left and right, as viewed from the pile of boulders looking towards Rebel Without a Pause.
sections.Getting There: See parent area for approach instructions. The lower level is reached first. Continue past all of the climbs in the lower level and scramble up some boulders to reach this area.

sections.Description:
This is the upper level of the Black Corridor, separated from the lower level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble.  

 These routes are on the left side, as viewed from the pile of boulders looking towards Rebel Without a Pause.
sections.Getting There: The wall on the left (southwest) side of the upper level.

routes.name: Thermal Breakdown

sections.Description: Good moderate usual Black Corridor route with a crux up high to pull the bulge before the anchors, the last bolt is kinda a awkward clip.  Good route worth doing.
sections.Location: This is the very first route on the left wall (East Facing) in the upper section of the Black Corridor and just 5 feet beyond the rock fall/blocks.  This and the next two routes (Crude Street Blues & Crude Behavior) are very similar.
sections.Protection: Route has 6 Bolts to some fixed anchors and your rappel!

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Crude Street Blues

sections.Description: Thermal Breakdown, Crude Street Blues, Crude Behavior, Dancin' w/ a God... they're all right next to each other and all the same anyway.  Facing Rebel w/o a Pause, these are on the left side of the upper Corridor.
sections.Protection: A few bolts to a lower-off.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Crude Behavior

sections.Description: Thermal Breakdown, Crude Street Blues, Crude Behavior, Dancin' w/ a God... they're all right next to each other and all the same anyway.  Facing Rebel w/o a Pause, these are on the left side of the upper Corridor.
sections.Protection: A few bolts to a lower-off.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Dancin' with a God

sections.Description: Thermal Breakdown, Crude Street Blues, Crude Behavior, Dancin' w/ a God... they're all right next to each other and all the same anyway.  Facing Rebel w/o a Pause, these are on the left side of the upper Corridor.
sections.Protection: A few bolts to a lower-off.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Live Fast, Die Young

sections.Description: Another Black Corridor route, this time with the crux down low with one heck of a tricky mantel move.
sections.Location: This is the 5th route on the left wall (East Facing) in the Upper Black Corridor and only 4-5 feet to the right of Dancin' with a God.  Start the route on a small left facing flake and pull the difficult mantel about 10 feet up.
sections.Protection: 5 Bolts should find you at the fixed anchors for your rappel; stick clipping the first bolt on this route would be recommended.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Black Gold

sections.Description: The crux of this similar Black Corridor route is at the beginning and a stick clip might be in order.  Long ways between first and second bolts to so a tricky mantle is involved.  Good sport route but shorties might find some of the clips hard to reach!
sections.Location: This route is the 6th route on the left wall (East Facing) in the upper Black Corridor and only 5 feet to the right of "Live Fast"; begin at a small right facing flake.
sections.Protection: 5 Bolts will find you at the fixed anchors for your rappel!

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Texas Tea

sections.Description: This route is about 10a if starting to the right a couple feet and climbing up to the ledge to clip the first bolt; probably 10c/d if going directly under the first bolt.  Great route with consistent movement and some thin moves in the middle.  I recommend this route!!
sections.Location: This is the 7th route on the left wall (East Facing) in the upper Black Corridor area and the second route from the end.  Begins at a black wall with the first bolt on a small ledge about 9 feet up.
sections.Protection: The usual 5 bolts will find you at the fixed anchors for your rappel.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

routes.name: Fools Gold

sections.Description: Really fun route with a crux right after clipping first bolt (somewhat difficult clip at second bolt).  Seems like an aweful long ways to the third bolt but the climb is a tad bit easier going here.  Move toward the huge hueco at the top and pull the really fun bulge to finish out; really fun route!!
sections.Location: This is the last route on the left wall (East FAcing) in the upper section of the Black Corridor, can't miss it!
sections.Protection: 6 Bolts will have you seeing the chains on top for your rappel.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner. and Dave Sobocan, 1990

sections.Description:
This is the upper level of the Black Corridor, separated from the lower level by a pile of boulders and an easy scramble.  

 These routes are on the right side, as viewed from the pile of boulders looking towards Rebel Without a Pause.
sections.Getting There: The wall on the right (northeast) side of the lower level.

routes.name: Rebel Without a Pause

sections.Description: Perhaps the best route in the Black Corridor - it is the obvious line that sits at the mouth of the upper section.  It begins on a terrace then climbs up steep, heavily-chalked huecos.
sections.Protection: Four bolts to a lower off.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Livin' on Borrowed Time

sections.Description: This fun little route is the last one on your right when facing Rebel w/o a Pause and climbs past a very obvious crescent-shaped hold.  The first clip is tough.
sections.Protection: A few bolts to a lower-off.  Be careful on the first clip!

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Texas Lite Sweet

sections.Description: This is on the right wall, two routes right of Rebal w/o a Pause.  Climbs past 4 bolts to anchors under a  ceiling.  Decent route

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Lewd, Crude, and Misconstrued

sections.Description: This is the corner on the right-hand side of the upper Black Corridor (when facing Rebel w/o a Pause).  Ascend the corner (sandbag at 5.9), then step right w/ difficulty.
sections.Protection: Six or seven bolts to a lower-off.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Sandstone Enema

sections.Description:
This is a fun route that has all the business at the bottom. Crimp past the first two bolts at the bottom, and then enjoy the remaining four bolts to the top. 

 If you head too far left at the bottom the grade drops to 5.10+.
sections.Location: This is the third route up canyon on the upper right hand said.

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

routes.name: Oils Well that Ends Well

sections.Description: I love this route and IMHO is one of the better routes in the corridor.  The crux bottom is tough small crimpers and really cool 5.10 terrain for a long ways until one last thin crux again at the top!
sections.Location: This is the second route on the right wall (West Facing).  Start on the crack/ramp to the right for the first two clips and then move straight onto the very thin face!
sections.Protection: I believe it had 6 bolts to the fixed chains up top.  Pretty easy to set up a top tope from the 757 2X4 route to its right!

routes.fa: Jim Steagall, Kevin Sandefur, Chris Werner, and Dave Sobocan, Fall 1990

sections.Description:
This is a really fun climb that gets easier the higher you go. The crux involves a balancy corner about a third of the way up, and right below a small roofed edge. 

 The numeric name comes from the fact that it is a 7 bolt 5.7, and a section of a 2x4 plank was used to assist in the anchoring while the route was bolted. 

 **Note: One concern is that the anchors are set back behind the top of the climb, creating a lot of friction on the rope as you lower off. For very small climbers (kids) it can be almost impossible to get enough weight on the rope to get them back to the ground, resulting in some forceful down climbing.  As there are already numerous links on the chains above, the only likely solution would be to add another anchor bolt below the current anchors to reduce the rope drag.
sections.Location: This route is a new addition to the corridor, and a welcomed climb for novices who are not looking to start their day on a 5.9... As you climb above the dividing boulders that separate the lower corridor from the upper, this route is the first on your right, and climbs the right-leaning crack/ramp.
sections.Protection: 7 bolts to two anchors (one with extended webbing)

sections.Description: The Heat Wave wall is located in the uppermost part of the Black Corridor above the Corridor’s regular “upper” level. Its name is derived from the record high heat wave in the summer of 2024 during which time most of the crag was bolted. It’s got a few short, punchy routes mostly in the 5.10 range. It can be accessed from above by hiking down from the gully above the Black Corridor. This is the gully above Sweet Pain wall and crossed to reach Hunter S Thompson and Great Red Book areas. Or you can scramble up from the upper level. It gets late morning sun for a couple hours then shade all afternoon, and is mostly sheltered from the wind.
sections.Getting There: Either drop in by scrambling up past Sweet Pain Wall or approach from below by scrambling up past the upper level of the Black Corridor.

sections.Description: Left-most route. Start next to the low-angle, right-facing ramp on the left end of the wall. Climb the face next to the ramp trending leftward to a black-varnish bulge and short roof above. Climb over the roof and up low-angle rock to anchors on a ledge.
sections.Location: Left-most route.

sections.Description: Start next to the low-angle, right-facing ramp on the left end of the wall. Climb straight up the face to a black vanish bulge (crux). Pass the bulge to a slab with anchors above.
sections.Location: Second route from the left.

sections.Description: Start in the middle-left of the wall at a left-facing flake. Climb next to the flake passing a right-angling seam/crack through some black-varnish to a steep bulge above (crux). A high reach will gain the anchors.
sections.Location: Middle-left of the crag, third route from the left.

sections.Description: Start in the middle-right of the wall next to a scrub oak. Climb up to some honeycomb huecos with a scoop above. Climb out of the scoop on the right and back left to anchors in another scoop above. Note: the route was thoroughly cleaned, but watch for some sandy holds and crispy surfaces.
sections.Location: Middle-right of the wall, third route from the right.

sections.Description: Start just left of some large boulders on the right end of the crag. Climb up past a large hueco below a left-angling roof/bulge. Surmount the bulge and pass a blank section (crux) to the anchors above. Note: the route was thoroughly cleaned, but watch for some sandy holds and crispy surfaces.
sections.Location: Second route from the right, next to some large boulders.

sections.Description: Right-most route. Start on a large boulder on the right end of the crag. Climb up to the left of a big scoop next to the second bolt. Continue through steep, featured rock above to a smooth face with anchors. Note: the route was thoroughly cleaned, but watch for some sandy holds and crispy surfaces.
sections.Location: Right-most route, above some large boulders.

sections.Description: Probably as far east as you'll go in the first pullout, this is a tall wall of fantastic rock, largely hidden from the parking lot. Climbs range in style from a beautiful varnished chimney to a bouldery overhanging crimpfest and everything in between. Sort of like Civilization Crag's big brother.
sections.Getting There:
Approach to Civilization Crag. Continue up under the "slot" climbs, and follow cairns uphill and east through a break (see beta photos). Head straight east and you'll arrive at The Chasm, and once you're at that wall, continue down and around the formation until you arrive at a short steep slot. Up the slot, and you've arrived at the wall. ~20 minutes.
To trade a slightly longer and steeper approach for a shorter drive, approach from the Red Springs parking lot. Head past the Main Cluster boulders and then go right up the steep hillside. Once the hill levels out, continue contouring west towards the crag. See the map for details. ~30 minutes.

sections.Description: Climb the far left face of the short wall, dealing with awkward moves and sequences. Hard to read. Also has the worst rock at the crag (but still pretty good).
A short, bolted boulder problem. Climbs really sustained with hard clips. Expect thin and fingery moves through all three bolts. Would be a difficult onsight.
sections.Protection: Three bolts to anchors. Having the third draw hanging is a huge help.

sections.Description: Climb the arete and face in the corner in the midst of the three faces. Cool stemming options for the tall.
Climbs the beautiful varnish chimney in the corner right next to Three Mouths, Three Faces. Really stellar climbing at the grade on bulletproof rock.
Climb the left side of the main wall with slabby varnish to start and an overhang to finish. Not as straight forward as it looks.

One of the best sport climbs of its grade in Red Rock. Climb the slightly slabby first half on wonderfully solid varnish crimps to a nice rest, then climb the dead vertical second half around a discontinuous crack to the anchors.
Climbs great varnish through a thin move at bolt two, then continues along very enjoyably through a break, a bulge, and a slab to the anchor.

The furthest right line on the main wall. Dyno (or don't) to the first flat jug and pull up into a juggy, sandy flake. Fight straight up and over to some pretty good crimps, and deal with one thin move before pulling into the pod and a no hands rest. More steepness on pretty good holds takes you up and left and into the finish of Celestial Spheres. Good fun.
The lefthand route on the lower wall. Climb through the initial steepness on huge varnish jugs then work the slab, break, and vertical upper wall on lovely plates.
Climb the rib to a hollow, juggy flake, then make some thin slabby moves to gain the vertical varnish. Up the crimps and plates to the anchor.

Easy to see form the parking lot, the Civ Crag is marked by a huge northwest-facing varnished corner. Routes range from jugs on a slab to slightly overhanging, and the rock quality is excellent, comprising mostly of the beautiful brown varnish usually associated with canyon routes. Looking for a run of moderate climbs a step up from the crowds at the Panty Wall and Magic Bus? This is the crag for you.
sections.Getting There: Head down to the right where the main trail initially splits, and then head up through a break to the right of Circus Wall.  From there, head east, keeping approximately even in altitude - you'll be almost paralleling the loop road. You'll cross a wash or two, and eventually you should spot the black, NW-facing backside of the crag, sitting below the large steep slab that is the Black Hole. 10-15 minutes from the parking lot.

sections.Description: This route starts on the left arete on the prow of rock to the left of the main wall. Climbs the interesting varnished face to the last bolt, then work up about 12' of fun slabby finger crack to anchors.

This route is located on the south facing wall in the slot to the left of the main crag. The leftmost line; climb the varnish slab to a small break, then work the thin vertical section past the last bolt to the anchors.
This route is on the south facing wall in the slot to the left of the main crag. The center line; climb the varnish slab to the last bolt, and then pull the overhang on huge jugs to the anchor.

This route is located on the south facing wall in the slot to the left of the main crag. The rightmost line; reach across to two huecos and climb over a little roof up the varnish slab to two juggy flakes. Use these to pull the overhang and arrive at the anchors.

The route climbs the left hand line on the tallest part of the main wall. Work the arete and the face  barely right on small crimps up the vertical wall for three bolts, and then enjoy the near vertical 5.8 face to anchors.

Climbs the center line on the tallest part of the main wall. Step across to two good crimps, then work straight up the vertical varnish face along a series of breaks. Work through the break and onto the high angle slab above, and work this to the anchor.
The right route on the tall part of the main wall. Step across into the chimney and work it for a bolt, then pull left onto the face and up past a small bulge and four more bolts to anchors.
The most center route on the main wall. Pull up onto the face to the right of the chimney, and work up past bolts to a big break with a massive horn of rock. Step above this and head to the anchors.

Splitter at a sport crag. Reminiscent of Yin+Yang but thinner, more smearing, and much smaller pro. A good excuse to visit Civilization Crags and the best rock on the cliff. Not much real crack climbing on this one, more of a V3/4 boulder problem with good gear, but it's an exciting line that will reward those that are adept at placing pro quickly from smears. Worthwhile.
sections.Location: The arching thin splitter above an offwidth flare sandwiched between Babylon 5.8 and Conquistador on the right side of the main wall. Shares anchor with Conquistador.
sections.Protection: Cams tiny to #4, exact beta would kinda ruin the fun. Bringing 2 #00 TCUs is a good idea, I used a #9 nut but it's very optional. No long slings or trickery, just a few cams added to your sport kit.

sections.Description: Climbs the blank looking far right face of the main wall. Pull up through underclings and sparse feet to the first bolt, then crimp up to another undercling. Work the crimps to the right of the prominant flake to the last bolt, then traverse left into the flake. A few moves and the chains are yours.

Fun little route that follows up the back side of Civilization.  Can face climb with ample protectability, or slot yourself into a series of three chimney/small hands cracks.  Not worth a hike in for, but if in the area and itching for a lil crack action, may be worth hitting up.  Definitely must have been others who have done it before, but adding it because it's such a perfect moderate route with already placed chains for easy rap. 

NOTE*  This route needs quite a bit of TLC and cleaning.  Lots of fragile rock, be careful and mindful of rock quality for protection.
sections.Location: From civilization wall, walk around right of the prominent arête.  Follow the first moderate crack on the left that starts in a small chimney or follow up the cruiser seam on the slab on the right to enter the crack above the chimney.
sections.Protection: Standard rack to #4 C4.  End at a juicy belay ledge that eats up small cams for anchor.  The belay ledge sits directly above Conquistador, so can easily rap off of those rings which are within arms reach from belay ledge.

sections.Description:
Lots of variety on this one. Start at the toe of the buttress on the southwest face, just right of the wide crack. Climb up the ramp to a high first bolt. Continue up to the steep head-wall to a well protected crux. Above, climb easy but more run-out slab to the higher, left anchor.
Don't top-rope or lower through the fixed anchors if someone else is climbing it, just the last person!
It's easy to use this anchor to TR the crack route to the left for a bonus pitch.
sections.Location: First bolted route from the left on the southwest face. Just right of the wide crack Meerkat Manor. Glue-in bolts.
sections.Protection: 8 bolts + 2 bolt anchor with mussy hooks = 10 bolts total.

sections.Description:
Starts 40 feet right of the arete separating the main northwest face of Civ from the southwest face. Climb the slab to a break where a few steeper moves on huge jugs take you back to slab climbing up and left to anchors. 
 The inconsistent face directly below the anchor can be climbed at a mellow 5.3, save for 10 feet of steep 5.8 terrain.
sections.Location: On the southwest face, the furthest left bolted line.

sections.Description: This route starts ten feet to the left of The Three Kingdoms at an obvious (mediocre) hand crack. Follow this crack until it ends at a mantle. Traverse right and finish The Three Kingdoms (3b's).
sections.Location: 10 feet to the left of The Three Kingdoms at an obvious hand crack.

sections.Description: Climbs to the highest point on the southwest face via some slab, some near vertical climbing on large varnish plates and jugs, with a large break about halfway up. Climbs like a gym climb.
sections.Location: Starts about 10 feet right of an obvious crack and flake system; the middle bolted line on the southwest face of the formation.

sections.Description:
Silk Road offers fewer big holds and more slab climbing than the rest of the routes in the area. Good for footwork. Well protected down low and where it's harder, and just a bit spacier when the climbing is easy - good for your mental game.
Don't top-rope or lower through the fixed anchors if someone else is climbing it, just the last person!
Give your rope a good pull from the right to avoid getting caught in the giant flake.
sections.Location: Second route from the right on the southwest face. Just left of Super Tsardom 5.4.
sections.Protection: 7 bolts + 2 bolt anchor with mussy hooks = 9 bolts total.

sections.Description: Start on the very blunt arete and follow the boltline up the mellow slab on large holds. Super chill.
sections.Location: On the arete separating the southwest and southeast faces of the formation.

sections.Description: Climb the near vertical wall on a ton of huge jugs. The crux comes pulling over a small overhang. Climbs like a gym route.
sections.Location: Route furthest left on the southeast face of the formation.

sections.Description: Climb the near vertical wall and through an overhang on massive jugs to the shared anchor with Five Charter Oath. Climbs like a gym climb
sections.Location: Middle route on the southeast face of the formation.

sections.Description: Climb the vertical plated wall for three bolts and a big no hands rest, then work up the steepness. After a few moves the angle eases and the chains are nigh.
sections.Location: Route furthest right on the southeast side of the formation.

sections.Description: Squeeze chimney.  Climbs gets a little narrow at the top but the crack can be exited from side nearest to the Umayyad Caliphate climb.
sections.Location: Right behind Umayyad Caliphate.
sections.Protection: Wide crack no pro, but can be TR'd.

sections.Description: The wall gets sun from mid morning on. Steep gray wall with several good routes.
sections.Getting There: Head straight downhill from the parking lot to the base of Circus Cliff. Head up slabs and boulders at the right end of that wall. After crossing a gully and hiking up a short slab/slope, the crag will be on your left and directly left of a large drainage. 10 minutes.

sections.Description: Climb up steep black varnish using a left-angling, corner-apex rail to a tricky pull onto a small ledge. Mantle above onto the sloping ledge, then climb-walk about 30’ to an 8’ wall. Climb up the short wall onto another ledge with the steep headwall above. Climb the headwall through jugs and crimps to a lower-off anchor. Good, fun climbing where it's vertical, but a bit let down by the low-angle slab in-between.
sections.Location: On the left end of the crag, start just inside the curve of the Cactus Corridor (right side).

sections.Description: Climb up black varnish to a mantle onto the sloping ledge, then climb-walk about 30’ to an 8’ wall. Climb up the short wall onto another ledge with the steep headwall above. Climb the headwall through jugs and crimps to an anchor just above a scoop. Be mindful of some soft rock in the scoop. Good, fun climbing where it's vertical, but similar to other routes in this section of the wall, a bit let down by the low-angle slab in the middle.
sections.Location: On the left end of the crag, start just before the wall starts to curve into becoming the corridor.

sections.Description: The climb starts on the varnished slab left of "Cactus Juice". Follow the line of bolts up the well varnished wall to a low angle slab. At the top of the slab, climb up and into a shallow corner/crack/flake system,. Follow the crack/flake up and slightly left to the anchors.
sections.Location: 10' left of "Cactus Juice"

sections.Description: Climb starts on the varnished wall just left of "Peyote and the magic stairs" on the far-left end of the Cactus Massacre Crag. Follow the line of bolts up the steeper lower wall to a low angle slab, up and slightly right to a steep headwall, (the crux) and the anchor.
sections.Location: 8' - 10' left of "Peyote and the magic stairs".

sections.Description: Follow the obvious stairway to a short slab, climb slightly up to the left of the small overlap and back right to a final steep wall to the anchor
sections.Location: 30' - 40' left of "Cactus Hugger", find the obvious stairway on the right left end of the Cactus Massacre Crag

sections.Description:
On the left side of the crag, just off the ground, are a series of body-length, left-facing flakes. Follow bolts up the center of the flakes (mind some soft rock) and onto a low-angle section to reach the vertical wall above. Climb the vertical wall through some nice varnish for a couple moves to the anchors above.
Note: new route as of Jan 2024, expect some suspect rock until the route cleans up further.
sections.Location: On the left side of the crag near a large 10' boulder. Look for the body-length, left-facing flakes.

sections.Description:
The left side of the wall has a cascading series of ledges with 10-15' sections between them. Start at a left-facing corner that cuts through the first ledge about 10' up. Climb the corner and mantle onto the ledge, then climb the steep wall to the next big ledge. Follow bolts up the easier middle section to the final ledge, then up the varnished-wall to the anchors. It's basically a series of boulder problems with rest ledges between them.
Note: new route as of Jan 2024, expect some suspect rock until the route cleans up further.
sections.Location: On the middle-left side of the crag look for a highly featured, left-facing corner behind a tall, scraggly Cat's Claw bush. This is at the base of an obvious series of ledges going up the wall.

sections.Description: Climb up onto the ledge, a few steep moves on jugs on the left seam\headwall, lead to a slab and rest. Climb up, slightly right, on ever steepening, beautiful black varnished rock, to a bit of a crux near the top.
sections.Location: This route start off a ledge, approx., 6-8' high. Its, (currently) the last bolted route on the left side of the wall, approx. 30' left of "Straight to the Point". There is another route that starts off this ledge, in the shallow corner.

sections.Description: A, or the, crux comes quick on this route. Climb the shallow corner\crack up past a 2 bolts, climb up, slightly right through a notch in an overlap. Continue up to the varnished, plated wall to a seam\crack system that leads straight up to the another crux just below the anchor.
sections.Location: This route starts on a 6-8" high ledge on the left hand end of the Massacre. There are 2 routes that start off this ledge, this one starts in a shallow corner. You can stick clip these routes from the ground.

sections.Description:
Start at a short, shallow cave/scoop on a ledge 3' off the ground. Mantle onto the sloping ledge above the cave/scoop and get into the business on steep crimps interspersed with good horizontal slots. Above the steepness, mantle the overlap and head up the vertical wall to the anchors.
Note: new route as of Jan 2024, expect some suspect rock until the route cleans up further.
sections.Location: Located left-center of the main face in-between the two prominent crack lines (Cactus Pete and Straight to the Point). Look for a shallow cave/scoop just off the ground with a bolt above it leading to a sloping ledge and steep wall above.

sections.Description: Just like the name says, this route wastes no time getting to it! Climb the side by side, steep seams in the dark rock on good jugs, pinches, and edges to a steep face. Continue up the seams on super fun moderate steep face\slab to a 5.8 overlap\roof. Once over come, a fun romp up 30' feet of easy slab.
sections.Location: The route starts just left of the light colored, steep, center wall. It is the 1st route in the dark rock, (it has glue ins) left of the steep light colored wall.

routes.name: Cactus Massacre

sections.Description: Start below steep gray wall in center of the cliff.
sections.Location: Center of the cliff

routes.fa: Paul Van Betten, Mike Ward, and Sal Mamusia, Dec 1987

sections.Description: Probably the best route on the cliff with a pumpy finish and difficult clip at the anchor.
sections.Location: The obvious crack that goes up the middle of the face. I have no idea why this wasn't bolted years ago as it seems like the most obvious line on the cliff.

routes.name: Cactus Root

sections.Description: Climb up pockets to join a left facing corner. Climb the corner, then head up the steep wall(3b's) into an overhanging seam which leads to the top.
sections.Location: Start 20' left of "Cactus Killa", or 20' right of "Cactus Massacre"

routes.fa: Paul Van Betten, Sal Mamusia, and Jim Olsen, Dec 1987

sections.Description: Start climb just right of, (or just climb the start of) Cactus Root, Clip the righthand bolt, (glue in), follow line/bolts up and slightly left through the light colored rock, (jugs), then up through the steep darker varnished rock, (crux), and up to chain anchors just up and left of the blunt arete.
sections.Location: This route climbs the left side of the steep, lighter colored wall, down low, then through the varnished, overhanging section up and slightly right. It is located just right of the center wall and Cactus Root, 5.11d. It's the next route left of Cactus Killa.

sections.Description: This route is fun from the start to the finish. Start on the crack in middle of the crag, gain holds on the steep face on the right. climb up through a technical crux, (1st - 2nd bolts). jugs lead up the ever steepening wall to the roof, good holds lead you up and left, then back right to the anchors.
sections.Location: The route starts in the middle of the crag, on the obvious wide, left angling crack at the base of the wall. 20' right of "bbCactus Root".

routes.name: Cactus Head

sections.Description: Climb a left facing corner to its top. Move right over a bulge and finish up the corner above.
sections.Location: Starts 10 feet left of Over a Barrel. Obvious corner\zigzag crack system on right end of cliff.

routes.fa: Paul Van Betten and Don Welsh, Dec 1989

sections.Description:
This climb starts on the obvious large Heucos on a small blunt arete right of "Cactus Head". A few steep and pumpy moves lead to a shallow corner, then straight up a headwall, (the lower crux), which sets you up for a nice seated rest on the sloping ledge above. The rest may be needed to tackle the large over-hang above that guards the anchors. 
Climb up off the ledge on large unique left-downward slanting \sloping edges to the roof. Climb up and slightly right, easier, (go left for big holds, steeper hero fun) then hand traverse back left for 8-10' on good holds and one final move to the anchors.
sections.Location: This climb start 10' right of the obvious zigzag trad crack, "Cactus Head".

routes.name: One Flew Over a Cactus Nest

sections.Description: Like its neighbor to the right, this route has a really fun, slightly technical start, with interesting climbing up to, (and beyond) the definitive crux just above mid-height on the route.
sections.Location:
This route starts approx. 15' left of "Never kiss a Cactus".
