Start on the series of flakes and edges in a slightly shallow corner. Climb up and slightly right thru a shallow slot in an overlap, to a slab and the headwall, (crux), continue up and slightly left to anchors.

sections.Description: Fun, thoughtful climbing leads to a definitive crux near mid-route
sections.Location:
15' left of "End of the Cactus", Climb the left facing corner, (use a long, (alpine), draw
 on fourth bolt), a fun hold rich ramp leads to the crux,.

sections.Description:
A really fun climb up the obvious blunt arête.

Trend toward the right mid-route rather than traversing left to the anchor visible from the ground, as that anchor is for the neighboring route. The last bolt before the anchors is a "mini chimney." This section is a bit exposed but very secure once you're on it.
sections.Location: Obvious blunt arête on right end of crag
sections.Protection: 6 glue in bolts to lower-off anchors.

sections.Description:
This crag was previously considered part of the Viagra Towers area and had a few TR-only routes and some trad climbs. In 2022, many new routes were bolted.
The south side is in the shade all day and the north side is shaded for some of the day depending with routes you climb. It’s also in the canyon and surrounded with walls on both sides so there is very little wind. The area is very open for belaying and child friendly. The types of climbs range from slab/tech climbing to pumpy and huecoed. If any new routes are added, please continue the parody music trend that the wall is following. Tortuga Tower is nearby and can be easily combined with a day of climbing here.
sections.Getting There: It’s about 5 mins from the parking lot of Calico Pull out. Once you come down the stairs, stay to the right and walk towards the Viagara tower. It’s another 300 feet beyond that to the East. In the book, this has a little of the fifty-five wall on it but since a new amount of routes are being added to this area and it’s getting developed, this is the name being given since the climbing route names have a trendy name that goes with the name of the wall (spoiler…. Think musical songs before the 2000s and make them into rock climbing parodies).

sections.Description:
This section faces south/southwest and is sunny most of the day, though the routes have slightly different aspects and some will get some shade depending on time of day/year.
The first two routes are on the end of the same wall as Viagra Towers outside the corridor. The next routes are inside the corridor on the left side.
sections.Getting There: See parent area for instructions. This is the left wall when approaching from the parking.

sections.Description: AC/DC might do dirty things but they never did this route to enjoy the dirty clings.  Enjoy the sweet climb through the large huecos.  The moves are amazing but the holds are a little sandy (yes I cleaned them as much as possible but more climbing will help).  Once you get through the 5.9 climbing huecos (stop at the last one and take a rest in it), you hit the crux of tech climbing.  Don’t worry, if you blow the move, the bolt is almost at your waist so you don’t have much of a fall.  Since this route is new, a helmet is suggested since there are some loose rocks still that someone will somehow find and pull off even if we cleaned off everything we think is around the path.
sections.Location: This is the furthest left of all the routes before you go into the gully of Classic Rock Wall. It’s one of the.m two routes in the left with large huecos that define the route.

sections.Description: Another AC/DC tribute, imagine being on a sweet route with huecos leading you to a section of bare wall climbing.  It’s like you on a highway having a great time and now you are in hell.  This route has smaller huecos (with a couple great knee bars)and some amazing monos.  After you cruise through the last hueco which is your last rest, you need get through the more blank section with some rails you can use to get to the last bolt and finish out.  This route is cleaner than it’s neighbor and has been favored out of the two despite it being harder.
sections.Location: It is on the left side of the wall when you come into the gully to the  right of Dirty Clings and has 3 distinctive small huecos with a bunch of monos in between the huecos. The crux is after the last hueco with some hidden holds that get you to the last bolt.

sections.Description:
*This route has had some rocks break on it since it’s newer and the holds are more hidden so wear a helmet until this route is cleaned better*
The Backstreet Boys would be proud because route didn’t seem possible when it was started.  Right away holds were breaking at the base but then the higher the route went, it cleaned up fast.   The hidden flakes that you can’t see until you are on the climb help provide a really relaxing climb until you hit the crux which is towards the end of the climb.  This is an amazing climb despite it looks intimidating and is very relaxed as long as you don’t fight the layback.  Also the rock tells you to go one way but ironically….. after the start you go another way.  One important thing with this route, I didn’t clean to the extreme left of the route so there is a lot of choss there.  Belayer should wear a helmet on this until the path is obvious to how to climb this.
sections.Location: When you walk into the valley/canyon, it’s with the routes on the left side (north side) and furthest to the left of the routes inside the valley.  There’s 3 small huecos towards the top of the route
sections.Protection: 5 bolts and permadraws at the top

routes.name: I Would Climb Any-cling for Love

sections.Description: Would Meatloaf truly do anything for love? Cause I bet he won’t do that.  This route has a lot of 2 fingered pockets at the start of the route that help you make your way up to one of the cruxes which involve a couple small hueco/pocket that you hold yourself on to make the clip and the optional small mono/pocket to the right.  Then you make your way up to the ledge and up the last large hueco only to discover your last crux on a hold which feels questionable.  Guess it’s time to find out.
sections.Location: It’s on the left side (north side) when you enter the gully and is the tallest of the routes and has a large hueco on the ledge where the anchors are.

sections.Description: Think Coolio has what it takes to live this life?  Try this route and find out.  Tons of amazing moves with a variety that truly makes this feel like a paradise climb.  Enjoy the large hueco that you can fit your entire body in and then to the crux that makes you appreciate the tight bolting.  This is one of the most enjoyed routes from what people have done at the wall so far.
sections.Location: It’s part of the group of routes on left side (north side) of the gully full of huecos.  This is the route to the right of I Would Climb Anything for Love

sections.Description: Start in a crack for about 30 feet, then ramble through very easy low angle, then finish up the face for 40 or so feet placing in the occasional horizontal. Descend off a 2 bolt anchor at the edge slightly left of the top out. Or top out and find a gear anchor far back on the ledge to belay your second up and scramble off?? We just used the bolted anchor. *Requires a 70m rope. Holds are very crispy, doesn’t seem like it’s had much traffic, pretty fun though. If you FA’ed this feel free to claim it.
sections.Location: Furthest right most documented route currently on the left wall. Just past a gully and directly across from Don’t Stop Belaying.
sections.Protection: Standard rack to a 2 bolt anchor with chains.

sections.Description: The routes inside the corridor face northeast and are generally shaded most/all day with just a bit of morning sun on longer days. The rightmost routes (Oops I Sent It Again to Sweet Climb O' Mine) are outside the corridor and face southwest, getting some sun from mid-morning on, and the leftmost route (Pretty High for a Climb Guy) faces south and gets sun until the late afternoon.
sections.Getting There: See parent area for instructions. This is the right wall when approaching from the parking.

routes.name: Pretty High for a Climb Guy

sections.Description: And all the tourists’ say Pretty High for a Climb Guy but make sure you take Offspring’s word and climb this route.  Start the route going between the flake on the right and slab on the left.  Press up into the crack……aretish climb and show your technical skills cause your muscles won’t do much on this route.  With a tight bolting setup through the large crack, you feel confident that you got through the crux but now cross onto the main rock and continue your way through the crimp slab.  Finally you see the end in sight, a long fun out of 5.5 to the anchors.  Clip in and turn around…. Enjoy the beautiful view facing the eastern canyon towards Las Vegas.  Beware the rope drag if you choose to top rope.
sections.Location: At the very end of the canyon of routes, come around the corner and you’ll see the bolts going up crack/arete.
sections.Protection: 11 bolts and mussy/permadraws at the top.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld, Julia Parrot and Katie Johnson

sections.Description: Climb up some fist-sized huecos and crimps to a steep bulge about 30' up (crux). After the bulge it's significantly easier ground to anchors.
sections.Location: At the end of the main corridor's wall, just before you turn the corner. Next route to the left of Hanging Fifty.

routes.name: Hanging Fifty

sections.Description: Start with a few hard crimps and then you can fly up the lie-back crack until the angle change. Continue through the slab with crumbling holds.
sections.Location: Far left of wall obvious crack/lie-back after small hold start.

routes.fa: Jay Foley, Donna Longo, and Milan Foley, Spring 2015

routes.name: Truly Chossy Gri-gri

sections.Description: This route may be your dream or fantasy but hold on tight (literally) and find out.  Highly recommend stick clipping if you are projecting around the low 11 mark.  Getting to the first bolt can be tricky and requires good foot work and a sidepull that doesn’t feel good until you get to the side of it.  Then the crux happens right after the bolt and going for a crimp rail and then to another forcing the 2nd clip.  There’s a reason the bolt was placed high on this one, so you didn’t have to work around the rope.  Get through the main crux and now run the slab portion up to the next wall section and work your way through the last challenge.  Careful not to Z clip the 2 bolts when on the second wall.  Once again, they were placed to ensure people didn’t deck if a hold broke.  Work your way through the sharp holds and the anchors are just above.  *This route does not endorse Gri-gri in any way or form*
sections.Location: About 30 ft to the left of Bolt Climb Rock and Fall and Climbing on Broken Choss.  Has a high first bolt.  On top of a rock sticking out of the ground and the 2nd bolt is right above a “blank” section in the rock.
sections.Protection: 8 bolts? Might be 7 and permadraw/mussy anchors at the top

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Julia Parrot

routes.name: Bolt Climb Rock and Fall

sections.Description: Bob Seger will tell you this route will help soothe the soul with all the different styles rolled into it.  It shares the same first bolt with Climbing on Broken Choss.  After you get up to the second bolt, you run into the crux but you are able to clip before committing into the crux and deciding how you want to tackle it from there.  Once through the crux you get some slab climbing and a nice rest before going into the face climb which is the cherry of the route.  You have a a combination of crack, hueco (body sized), knee bar and lastly plates that you get to use to work your way up to the anchors.  Once through, you get one more little slab and to the anchors. Oh and like Broken Choss, you wonder if the holds are gonna break but they are durable for some odd reason.  Enjoy the rush and different styles and make your way up this route that will help you reminisce about the most important part to climbing…… fun.
sections.Location: Shares the same first bolt with Climbing on Broken Choss and then breaks right into a distinct crack and large human sized hueco.
sections.Protection: 10 bolts and mussy/permadraws at the top.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld, Julia Parrot and Katie Johnson

sections.Description: Maybe Annie Lennox would have get better after her break up if she had climbed this route….. or maybe not.  Crux is around the 2nd bolt with trusting whichever style you choose to get through it (theres about 3-4 different holds but nothing distinctive like a huge jug but maybe a sloper or a crimp or a spot way up where you can put your right hand in and fist lock).  Then it eases up once you get through it into 5.9 climbing the rest of the way up. But if you notice the bolting, it looks tight suggesting a crux but there isn’t mainly because the holds seem fragile but something about that rock is insanely strong on the south side (maybe more iron in the rock or etc?) and doesn’t break off easily.  So keep climbing, get that weird feeling on while completing that section and enjoy the nice 5.6 run out at the top to the anchors.
sections.Location: To the immediate left of Unbreak my Hold, down in the gully.  Has a distinctive small hueco about 2/3rd the way up the route that’s about the size of a grapefruit.

routes.name: Un-break My Hold

sections.Description: Toni Braxton wants you to unbreak the holds that you might cause on this route since there’s a lot of nice holds on this route which are extremely strong thanks to the varnish.  The start is probably the hardest part to this route since you actually start to the right of the first bolt and make your way towards the bolt to clip.  Then from there it’s up into a lot of sharp holds with a tight bolt line that makes you think there’s a crux there but there really isn’t.  Why is it bolted that tight? Well at the 2nd tight bolt there’s a hold that sounds hollow but is solid and strong (tried to break it and it wouldn’t give and held my weight) so to be safe, put a bolt near it and if it breaks then the bolt line is ready for the new crux to come.  A great route with great holds.  Wear a helmet if you are concerned.
sections.Location: It’s on the right side (south side), down the gully about 25 ft after “Pour some Beta on Me” and you can see the bolts in the black varnish and the anchors on a large varnish plate that sticks out in the rock

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Aaron Delaundreau, 2022

routes.name: Pour Some Beta On Me

sections.Description: Def Leppard will tell you that this route is definitely a challenging slab that will make you want to figure out the beta. The major crux is in the beginning now when one of the nice holds that made it a 11a broke and now it’s a very technical face climb start but then as you work your way up the route.  The true (before the break) crux stands out distinguished by the tight bolting on a rather blank face that slopes inward giving your hands relief but your feet…. not so much.  Well protected and a challenge that isn’t pumpy, what more can someone ask for other than a longer crux.
sections.Location: It’s to the left of “Don’t Stop……. Believing” which is on the right side (south side) of the gully. Starts in the middle of the wonderful Nevada shrubbery that are always angry and don’t like to be touched.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Aaron Delaundreau Feb 2022

routes.name: Don’t Stop Belaying

sections.Description: Journey would tell you to don’t stop….. believing in how much fun this slab route is.  It’s a laid back tech climb that makes you wish it keeps going.  There’s 2 cruxes in the route that make you commit your feet to the cause.  Start the route by clipping the first clip off the big rock (literally stick clip without the stick) and then work the crack to the right and then commit over to the next bolt once you get above the first bolt then begin the fun climbs.
sections.Location: After going by the routes on the left side (north side), there’s a gully that goes up the left and this route is on the right side after that and there’s a gigantic rock coming out of the ground.  That’s the rock you can clip the route off of and it’s to the left of a crack.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Adam Schenk, Feb 2022

sections.Description: Start on the pink boulder and layback the low crux. Low quality rock up the crack/chimney.
sections.Location: The wide crack system just right of Don’t Stop Belaying.
sections.Protection:
Standard rack, some larger sizes may be useful. Bolted anchors.
This route existed prior to the bolts of Don’t Stop Belaying, but the first bolt on that route can now be used to help protect the start.

sections.Description:
Hush little climber, climb the corner, and never mind that noise you heard, it’s just the rock slipping in your hand, you fall backwards, there goes the send!
A fun foot tech route that starts kind of in a corner.  Use that corner and stem your way up to the first bolt and then follow the line from there being surrounded by sandstone on the top, right side and underneath. Lots of options to use but some delicate footwork if you are learning to trust your feet more.  Eventually, you are towards the top and there’s nothing foot worthy but just smear and enjoy that your feet stay in place.
This is also tightly bolted so it’s another good route to help someone work using their feet and not have to worry about falling.  Also this route is torn between a high 8 and low nine, so let MP know what you feel the grade is. 
*New route of 02/2026 so wear a helmet until it's cleaned up.  Tried to break and yard as much as I can but this route is NOT in the sun ever and rain doesn't dry out as fast so give it plenty time for the rock to dry.
sections.Location: Between Don’t stop belaying and Wannabe.  There’s a large rock next to the start and it’s in the corner and you’ll notice the bolt line goes up into a corridor.
sections.Protection: 10 bolts and mussy clips at the top

routes.name: Wannabe (my belayer)

sections.Description:
*route update* 2nd bolt was place between the now 1st and 3rd bolt making it safer and less run out.  Bolt was placed on 1/30/25
So I’ll tell you want I want, what I really really want.  The Spice Girls want a fun slab climb with moves that can make you go ahhhh.  This is a great climb and has some neat moves you can pull climbing it along with using as much of the surrounding rock as you can (as shown in the pictures).  Work your way up through the features and make it to the top.  There was a set of anchors up there before and assuming it’s for the crack way to the right (couldn’t lower on them though cause they have no rap rings or anything) so that route can be done and lowered on as well if somebody wants to put it in the book.
sections.Location: To the right of Don’t Stop…… Belaying by about 30 ft.  Belay on the large rock sticking out of the ground.

routes.fa: Aaron Geistfeld and Aaron Delaundreau Feb 2022

sections.Description:
This is a more difficult, direct start to Fight for Your Right (To Onsight) which was done on TR before that climb was bolted.
Instead of walking up the ramp at the start of that climb, start immediately off the base of the ramp and boulder through cool, slopey dishes and crimps before moving into the easier shared finish through varnished terrain.
sections.Location: Start just left of Fight for Your Right (To Onsight) at the base of the ramp and tackle the full length of the pocketed wall.
sections.Protection: TR from the anchors of Fight for Your Right (To Onsight).

routes.name: Fight for Your Right (To Onsight)

sections.Description:
Your mom busted in and said, what's that noise? Aw, mom you're just jealous it's the Beastie Boys!
That’s right kids. You gotta fight for this one. Hard crux between bolt 4 & 5.
sections.Location: In the corridor on the right side, right of all the slabby routes. Up the steep belly to the varnished slab.
sections.Protection: 7 bolts to lower offs. Don't TR on fixed gear.

routes.fa: Gary Newmeyer, Japhy Dhungana, Brittany Venci - Oct 2024

routes.name: Sends in Low Places

sections.Description: What is a country song doing on a rock wall?!  Wel it’s this is actually about all forms of music so gotta give it to Garth to appreciate our short sends.  Starts out a to the right of the first bolt on some good holds and side pull yourself over to the first bolt, then make your way up through huecos and good holds.  Going through the midsection, there’s some rather questionable rock (Rock was tested and it held from being pulled on) which is the crux part.  After that, commit and it’s done.
sections.Location: About 30 ft to the left of Routebusters.  Right across from the path that takes you to the other 3 routes on the opposite wall.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Aaron Delaundreau

sections.Description: Ray Parker Jr is gonna call you to solve this route.  Work your way up the shallow huecos/pockets.  Enjoy the knee bar and then before you realize it, the crux is there and figuring it out may need to go back into the kneebar to relax.  Find the hold that will get you over the crux and then work your way up to the anchors. Join the routebusters crew and say…. I ain’t afraid of no holds!
sections.Location: It’s on the immediate right (south side) when you enter the gully into the wall almost on the arete.  You’ll see 3 large shallow huecos and a rather high first bolt but an easy climb to reach.

routes.name: Oops I Sent It Again

sections.Description: Want a route that will give you as much attention as Brittney Spears would get from the paparazzi?  This is the route for you!  It’s facing the parking lot and everybody will be watching you as you climb so it’s well bolted to ensure safety.  Start out with a nice jugs and foot holds onto a lot of little ledges and small handholds.   Good news is that is has a slabbish angle so you can really trust your feet and move forward through the crux.  Which is about a little less than half way up the route.  Once through it, it’s a fun climb to the small crack line on the left and up to the anchors which have permadraws on it.  This is a great starter route for those projecting and is very tight bolted to help gain comfort on small tech routes since there’s so many small options.
sections.Location: It’s on the immediate right before you walk into the gully. It’s in the sun from noon to the evening and one of the 2 routes facing the parking lot.
sections.Protection: 10 bolts plus permadraw anchors at the top

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Adam Schenk, Feb 2022

routes.name: Climbing on a Prayer

sections.Description: If you are a fan of letting people watch you climb a crimpy route that really doesn’t let up, then this the route.  Bon Jovi will tell you that Gina told Tommy to hold on to what they got on this route.  You are engaged the entire way up with small hand holds giving you some rest but not letting up on the hands.  Work your way from an amazing start at the first bolt up the crimp ladder til you hit the last bolt where it eases up and you clip into the anchors at the top.
sections.Location: On the right side before you enter into the gully and one of the two routes you will see and is to the right of  Oops I Sent It Again with a nice first bolt on a ledge. It’s facing the parking lot and you will have people looking at you while you climb but you will look awesome doing it.

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Adam Schenk Feb 2022

sections.Description: Start about 8' right of Climbing on a Prayer next to a bush/tree, below big undercling flakes about 10' up. Climb through the flakes and a steep section above (crux), then through a low-angle, shallow and wide corner to anchors just below a small roof/bulge.
sections.Location: On the right side of the wall facing the parking lot, next line to the right of Climbing on a Prayer.
sections.Protection: 6 glue-in bolts to pigtail lower-off anchor.

sections.Description: Start about 6' right of Another Bolt in the Wall, across from a small shade cave, below a 3' triangular roof about 20' up. Climb up to the roof and pass it on the left (crux) then another 20' of progressively easier climbing to the anchors.
sections.Location: On the right end of the wall facing the parking lot, next route to the right of Another Bolt in the Wall.
sections.Protection: 6 glue-in bolts to pigtail lower-off anchor.

sections.Description:
Three routes on a separate cliff above the main Classic Rock corridor. 

 This area is just beyond Upper Rift and can easily be combined with climbing there as well.
sections.Getting There:
From the main corridor, walk up a ramp just beyond Climber's Paradise. This wall is shortly after the top of the ramp. 

 Alternatively, continue past Upper Rift. This wall is a minute beyond and slightly below that one.

sections.Description:
Start at the low point on the left side of the wall. Climb up past a small rotten flake, then up to a black-varnish jug patch. Continue above the varnish patch to anchors in a slight bulge at the top.
First lead done solo: another lonely day, you can go your own belay!
sections.Location: Left-most route of the three bolted lines at the upper, left/west wall.

routes.name: Climber of 5.9

sections.Description: Brian Adams got his first 6 quick draws bought them at the REI and climbed this route til his fingers bled and became a climber of 5.9 (-).  But this is more of a techy slab route that has 2 distinctive cruxes.  Unfortunately like many of the other routes this doesn’t have as many hold options making it the hardest route on the wall.
sections.Location: This is on a wall that has 2 bolted routes and is the route on the left.  After you go by Climber’s Paradise, there is a gully that goes up to the left and you follow that to the wall.  It’s a nice spot that’s in the sun the entire day.
sections.Protection: 8 bolts and anchors with permadraws at the top

routes.fa: Aaron “The Batman” Geistfeld and Adam Schenk

sections.Description: Eagle Eye Cherry will tell you to get this route  because tomorrow you’ll be gone (if you are visiting Vegas).  Honestly this was a fun route that when you get to the crux, give that undercling a good pull to get you through the crux.  The good news is the bolt is right there to catch you so you won’t fall.  After that, its got pretty distinguished holds and good face climbing to the top.
sections.Location: This is the route to the right on the wall that has two routes.  To get here, go by Climber’s Paradise and follow the valley/gulley to the left up and you’ll see an open space there with 2 bolted routes about…. 100 yards up the valley.  These routes are always in the sun just to warn.
sections.Protection: 8 bolts? and permadraws at the top

sections.Description:
Broken face with a number of crack systems that provide some more moderate trad and TR options.
Southwest facing with sun from mid-morning on. Some wind protection due to its low position in the wash.
Though this are existed prior to all of the routes in the Classic Rock area, this is now just the leftmost end of Classic Rock Left (NE).
sections.Getting There: Head down the hill from the parking lot and take a right on a well-worn trail before reaching the wash. This trail eventually goes down to the wash as well at which point the wall should be obvious. Easy, 5 minute approach.

sections.Description: Well-protected corner.
sections.Location: Obvious corner on the left end of the formation.

sections.Description: Easy approach, barely used climbing area.
sections.Location: This route top ropes the front face of the pillar to the right of Viagra Corner.
sections.Protection: No bolts. Top rope class 3 scramble to anchor. Two hard to reach bolts just below the top of the pillar are used for anchor.

sections.Description: thin gear placement at start
sections.Location: right about 15' of Viagra Corner
sections.Protection:
~ standard rack 

 shared anchor at top of wall  (near a bush)

sections.Description: Easy approach, barely used climbing area.
sections.Location: Climb the thin crack and face in the middle of the wall.
sections.Protection: Top rope, no bolts. There is a strong bush to rap off to protect down climb to anchors.

sections.Description: No matter how you start, you end up in the crack and have a solid, clean route up.
sections.Protection: Two bolts anchor with a screw link to rap down from.

sections.Description: The crag includes a few distinct features: The Watchtower complex, the Alcove, and Lone Pine Wall. The Chasm was developed prior to the other walls but is directly below Lone Pine Wall and is essentially in the same area. It can be seen from the First Pullout up and beyond Civilization Crag if looking at it from the parking lot. Ratings will likely settle in with more traffic. Always advise wearing a helmet.
sections.Getting There: Best approached via the First Pullout. Follow directions for Civilization Crag then head up through the slot (slot has Mongol Hoarde-10a in it) to the left of the main Civilization crag--then through a bouldery notch at the top of this slot. On the other side of the notch, cross the gully then angle up left toward the Watchtower–roughly 5 minutes from the bouldery notch. Overall, approach takes 22 minutes at easy pace once you are familiar with the route. Following these directions will deposit you at the base of the Watchtower crag among several beautiful barrel and hedgehog cacti.

sections.Description: This area includes the steeper climbs up the gully to the left of Sand Whispers as well as climbs up to the right.
sections.Getting There: See approach for Watchtower under main area. Following the approach brings you to the base of Sand Whispers which follows the blunt rib/arête at the low base of the crag.

sections.Description: Warm up on big holds to a good stance before the steeper climbing starts. Crux in the lower middle followed by some cruisy climbing. Finish with devious climbing on short upper panel.
sections.Location: Currently furthest climb up the gulley to the left.

sections.Description: Start just left of low ledge and scramble up (bolt protected) onto sloping ledge with good stance. Good climbing leads to strenuous crux in middle on tricky feet. Tops out on left side of sloping ledge shared by Raven's Rune and Owl's Delight both to the right.
sections.Location: Start 8' to the right of Zephyr's Wing.

sections.Description: Starts on left side of low ledge clipping one bolt to gain the sloping ledge. Climb through parallel diagonal cracks to small black varnish recess. Pull through the small bulge above and gain sloping ledge shared by Crossfire to the left and Owl's Delight to the right.
sections.Location: 7' to the right of Crossfire.

sections.Description: Starts 10' right of Raven's Rune on right side of low ledge. Gain the ledge and wonder up until short steep section--crux. Clip bolt  and make tricky moves before last couple bolts.
sections.Location: 7' to the right of Raven's Rune

sections.Description: Clip the first two bolts (extend #2) of Owl's Delight then break right into the wide crack/chimney for 20' or so clipping 2 more bolts just left of chimney along the way. Gain broken ledge and climb towards the steep and imposing crack/seam above and to the right. Extension on bolts below steep section mitigates rope drag. Difficult climbing through two cruxes brings you to fun climbing through the last two bolts to the anchor.
sections.Location: Shares start with Owl's Delight.

sections.Description: Located 15' to the right of Owl's Delight/Harbinger shared start. Close to vertical for first couple of bolts leads to two short bulges before the broken ledge system. Scramble up broken ledge to steep upper headwall. Crux in final four bolts with steep climbing mostly on jugs.
sections.Location: 15' to the right of Owl's Delight/Harbinger shared start.
sections.Protection: 11 or so bolts plus mussy hooks

sections.Description: Located 10' right of Reaper. Starts just left of Watchtower in rounded corner. Challenging (crux) opening moves and difficult climbing through first few bolts lead up towards terrain just right of prominent upper corner. Upper crux is getting established on the black patina. Enjoy the outstanding position and climbing through the last 3-4 bolts to anchor.
sections.Location: Located 10' right of Reaper.

sections.Description: Perhaps the best route on the cliff, this line runs up the obvious prominent left leaning rib/arete on super cool holds. Starts with black slab/face to gain base of overhanging rib. Get established on rib (somewhat of a blind reach) and fight the pump for the next few bolts. Finish on good face holds up high for final 3 bolts.
sections.Location: 6' to the right of Overlord.

sections.Description: Bouldery start (through bolt 2) on thin black holds leads to lower angle slab. Move up on steep softer rock into the corner (crux?!) then up nice black rock. Surmount tricky bulge up high to gain the anchor.
sections.Location: 7' to the right of Watchtower.

sections.Description: Starts 7’ right of Sentry. Easy start up to steeper climbing just right of corner. Work up through technical climbing on good though not obvious slots/edges.
sections.Location: Starts 7’ right of Sentry

sections.Description: Starts slightly downhill to right of Zen Garden. Start just right of slabby prow. Crux in the middle on thin feet. Difficulty on this might vary if staying far left through crux.
sections.Location: Finding this climb is a great place to orient yourself upon arrival. It's at the low point of the main Watchtower crag with climbs up the gully to the left and climbs on the south facing portions of the crag to the right. There are several barrel and hedghog cacti nearby at the base. The climb follows the blunt arete feature.

sections.Description: Starts 7’ right of Sand Whispers. Scramble up easy terrain clipping one bolt if you choose to gain ledgy area just below steeper black rock. Climb up into shallow corner then up to anchors.
sections.Location: Starts 7’ right of Sand Whispers.

sections.Description: Starts up and right of Cactus Guardian on nice black rock. Climb up into the scoop and load up for crux on good holds. Solid climbing above eases off towards the top. Super fun climbing on this one!
sections.Location: 10' up and to the right of Cactus Guardian

sections.Description: Starts just up and right of Desert Alchemist. Move up into black rock on good holds. Pull through a small bulge on a steeper section then up towards the anchor on good holds.
sections.Location: Just up and right of Desert Alchemist

sections.Description: Just uphill and right of Wind Child. Clip the first bolt and step across the void (or step down and do direct start) then work your way up the featured rock.
sections.Location: 8' or so to the right of Wind Child. Also just right of obvious crack.

sections.Description: Starts 8’ right of Time Bender. Moderate climbing. Still a bit fragile.
sections.Location: Starts 8’ right of Time Bender

sections.Description: Fun moderate climbing on closely spaced bolts.
sections.Location: Up and to the right of Prickly Bandit there is a nice little flat hangout with a shorter panel. This little panel has three routes on it. Tomorrow Smiles is the leftmost of these three routes–roughly in the middle of the panel.
sections.Protection: 4-5 or so bolts plus mussy hooks.

sections.Description: Located  7’ to the right of Tomorrow Smiles. Starts on smaller crimps and finishes on slab above. Fun moderate climbing.
sections.Location: Located 7’ to the right of Tomorrow Smiles.

sections.Description: Located 7' to right of Moonlight Barrel. Up face to short slab before anchor. Short crux in lower section.
sections.Location: Located 7' to right of Moonlight Barrel

sections.Description: The Alcove (and Lone Pine Wall) sit just 50' or so to the right of the right most climbs at the Watchtower. The Alcove faces west and includes a steep slab that runs into a very narrow corridor to the right. The first two routes are on the slab. The next three to the right include one starting at mouth of corridor and two inside the corridor on the left side.
sections.Getting There: Follow directions for the main Watchtower approach and orient from there.

sections.Description: Pleasant edges and slab on closely spaced bolts lead to short steeper upper section on good holds.
sections.Location: Left most route on Alcove wall.

sections.Description: Pleasant edges and slab on closely spaced bolts lead to short steeper upper section on good holds.
sections.Location: 7' to the right of Joker.

sections.Description: Short crux at bulge.
sections.Location: 8' to the right of thief. Just before the mouth of the narrow corridor on the left side.

routes.name: There Must Be Some Kinda Way Outta Here

sections.Description: Chimney your way up until you can transition completely to the left side. Short crux at bulge before last bit to anchor.
sections.Location: Starts 10' to the right of Wildcat deep inside the narrow corridor on the left.

sections.Description: Short stemming section leads to mellow climbing on good holds to the anchor.
sections.Location: Last route on the left after squeezing your way through the narrow corridor. 10' to the right of previous route.

sections.Description: The Lone Pine Wall is the large west facing slab that sits down and right of the Alcove. This slab has a ledge system running along it. A beautiful pine tree is located on the left of the base of this slab.
sections.Getting There: Either follow the directions for the main Watchtower approach or approach as per the Chasm. The Alcove sits just left of the Chasm opening.

sections.Description: Start at the leftmost portion of the wall. Step across from big boulder cruising up moderate terrain. Steeper finish (crux) at last bolt before anchor.
sections.Location: Left most climb on the Lone Pine Wall--just down and right from the Alcove.

sections.Description: Fun flow with steeper start, cruiser middle, and steeper finish.
sections.Location: 10' right of Just your opinyon, man. Start off ledge.

sections.Description: Steep start with low crux. Like the route to the left, cruiser middle section with short steeper finish.
sections.Location: 10' right

sections.Description: Start off the ledge system. Low bolt for belayer. Three bolts protect steeper climbing in lower section (crux) to crack above. Crack requires gear up to .75.
sections.Location: Start is off far right of ledge system--10' right of previous route. Low bolt for belayer to clip in.
sections.Protection: 3 bolts plus a few pieces of small gear to .75".

sections.Description: Long fun pitch of moderate climbing including a few slab moves interspaced with slightly steeper bulges on good holds. A rope stretcher if you belay from lowest good stance--tie knot in end of rope. Should clean up quickly.
sections.Location: Starts 15' down and right of previous route. It's located on the far right side of the Lone Pine Wall and just left of the opening for The Chasm. Hard to see anchors but they are up there!

sections.Description: A massive chimney visible from the parking lot above and to the east of Civilization Crag. The wall faces southwest, but the chimney has shade almost all the time.
sections.Getting There: Approach to Civilization Crag. Continue up through the Civ slot, and traverse east and up through a fairly obvious break. Three more minutes on flat ground straight east brings you to the wall. 15-20 minutes.

sections.Description: Climbs the line on the left side of the chimney. Climb the steeper-than-it-looks wall through mostly great rock until the wall finally turns over to slab. Pumpy.
Climbs the dirty chimney at the back of the big beautiful chimney. Originally free soloed.

Climb the right side of the chimney up an improbable varnished face until you gain the arete, then angle up and left to the anchor. The early portion of the climb has a pair of moves that are surprising (and techy). Really cool.
Climb the right arete on big varnished jugs until it makes sense to pull over onto the slab. A few slabby moves brings you back to vertical and the anchors.

The Upper Rift area contains the routes past the boulder jam at the end of the Rift Corridor area. These are mostly short routes characterized by easy climbing to a punchy (and often steep) one or two move crux. The left side has easier routes, the middle has moderates, and the right side has the challenges. Morning shade, then sunny after about 10-11am.
sections.Getting There: Scramble past the boulder jam at the end of the Rift Corridor, or hike around the corridor itself on the right side passing under Bowling Ball wall.

sections.Description: Climb up the face next to the large boulders on the left. A thin start that is easy to make hard leads to straightforward climbing up the face.
sections.Location: Located immediately to the right of the large boulders that serve as the left end of the Upper Rift area.

sections.Description: Start about 6’ right of the big boulders, immediately left of a scrub oak #1. Climb up through the S-curve of rock texture (crux) and surmount a small bulge below the anchors.
sections.Location: Located next to the big boulders and scrub oak, the second route from the left.

sections.Description: Start immediately right of scrub oak #1. Climb the smooth, white rock to a hueco-smile below some varnish. Pass the hueco-smile on the left and continue up through the varnish to a steep bulge with the anchors. (The last route to stay in the shade in summer.)
sections.Location: Located between the first and second scrub oaks at the base of the wall, the left route. Look for a section of smooth, white rock with a hueco-smile about 10’ up.

sections.Description: Start immediately left of scrub oak #2, below a hueco-smile in smooth, white rock. Climb to the hueco-smile and pass it on the right. Continue up to a steep bulge (crux) guarding the anchors.
sections.Location: Located between the first and second scrub oaks at the base of the wall, the right route. Look for a section of smooth, white rock with a hueco-smile about 10’ up.

sections.Description: Climb up to a seam/crack that splits the steep bulge above. Continue along the seam/crack to the anchors.
sections.Location: Located between the second and third scrub oaks at the base of the wall, the left route. Look for the seam/crack splitting the steep bulge at the top of this wall.

sections.Description: Climb through some low varnish to a patch of splotchy red and white and bumpy rock. Continue through more varnish to the right end of the steep bulge guarding the anchors.
sections.Location: Located between the second and third scrub oaks at the base of the wall, the right route. Look for the right end of the steep bulge atop this section of the wall, just left of the wide, smooth valley of the route, Grave Peril.

sections.Description: Climb up slabby terrain to a steep section below a 4’-wide, smooth, shallow valley in the steep bulge above. Climb through this valley to low-angle rock that rolls over to a ledge. Continue above the ledge to the anchors.
sections.Location: Located immediately past the third scrub oak, a few feet left of the 2-foot block at the base of the wall.

routes.name: It's Tricky To Rock A Climb

sections.Description: Start next to a 2-foot block at the base of the wall and climb up passing the curving corner on the left. Continue up past a short, shallow, right-facing corner to easy slabby climbing to the anchor.
sections.Location: Located on the right side of the area, just left of a large curving corner on the left end of a ledge about 10’ up.

sections.Description: Climb up onto the ledge through a 2-foot mega varnish jug patch. Climb through a brown-varnish patch immediately off the ledge, and continue through a bulge to low-angle rock and the anchors. Caution: The geometry here makes for a rope-entangled fall near the brown varnish patch. It’s possible for the belayer to scramble up onto the right end of the ledge (below the route End On A High Note) to avoid the rope-entangling fall potential.
sections.Location: Located on the right side of the Upper Rift area. Look for a ledge with a swooping right-facing corner on its left end, and a brown-varnish patch.

sections.Description: Scramble/walk a few feet onto the right end of the ledge and climb the steep bulge to some good holds and crimps above. Continue up and slightly right to the anchors.
sections.Location: Located on the right side of the Upper Rift area. Look for the steep rock above the right end of the ledge with a swooping corner on its left end.

sections.Description: Start next to some boulders and reach up to the starting huecos. Pull through the huecos and onto the flakes above. Climb the flakes until they run out, then crimps to steep rock guarding the anchors.
sections.Location: Located on the far right end of the Upper Rift area. Scramble onto a ledge between a large vegetation patch (just right of End On A High Note) and a big, left-facing corner. On the left side of the ledge there are some boulders with a pair of huecos about 8’ up.

sections.Description: Start a few feet left of the corner at low-angle rock and climb up to the steep wall at a right-facing flake. Continue past the flake and crimp your way to the anchors.
sections.Location: Located on the far right end of the Upper Rift area. Scramble onto a ledge between a large vegetation patch (just right of End On A High Note) and a big, left-facing corner. Look for the bolts a few feet left of the left-facing corner.
